title: Product Lead, Acquisition and Activation
description:
About Us


At Félix, we are building the indispensable financial companion for Latinos in the US. We combine an AI-powered, conversational-first interface with real-time financial infrastructure to make cross-border money movement as easy as sending a text. Starting with fast, affordable remittances powered by AI and crypto rails, we are expanding into credit, savings, and wallet services to support the complete immigrant financial journey. Our ambition is to deliver a white-glove financial experience with the simplicity of a conversation to a community the traditional financial system has historically overlooked.

We are a hyper-growth Series C company, backed by over $300 million in funding from top-tier global investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, QED, Castle Island, Switch Ventures, HTwenty, Monashees, General Catalyst Customer Value Fund. This isn't just about the numbers; it's a testament to the trust our investors have in our vision and our team. Additionally, Félix was selected as an “Endeavor Entrepreneur” and was a recipient of the CrossTech Fintech Startups Award.

Joining Félix means you will be part of a team building a legacy, a company that will outlive us all. This is a rare opportunity to apply your skills to a deeply meaningful mission—serving a community that has been underserved for too long because we are obsessed with our customers. We get things done with urgency and focus, driven by extreme ownership over our impact. We collaborate without ego, fostering radical transparency and fierce loyalty so we can grow together. Because we aim for insanely great rather than just good enough, we stay insatiably curious—always experimenting, building the future today, and delivering a product that truly makes our users' lives better.



About the Role


As Product Lead for Acquisition and Activation, you will lead the cross-functional squad responsible for driving user acquisition and early activation across all of Félix’s consumer lending products.
In this role, you will own the end-to-end journey for acquiring "new-to-Félix" users through loan products, as well as optimizing first-loan conversion and the critical progression from first to second loan. Working across both new and existing user bases, you will establish reliable measurement frameworks for loan funnels, identify high-impact conversion barriers, and design scalable growth loops that balance rapid origination growth with strict credit-quality and unit-economic targets.

Responsibilities


  • Set Growth Direction & Strategy: Define the short-, medium-, and long-term strategy, OKRs, squad priorities, and roadmap for consumer lending acquisition and activation.
  • Own Acquisition & Activation Loops: Design, test, and scale growth loops that attract new users, maximize first-time borrower conversion, and drive progression to a second loan across all lending offerings.
  • Lead Discovery & Experimentation: Combine rigorous user research, funnel and cohort analysis, and unit economics to prioritize opportunities, launch continuous experiments, and scale winning tactics.
  • Lead the Pod: Provide clear direction, foster delivery excellence, and cultivate deep ownership and judgment across your cross-functional engineering, design, and data pod.
  • Cross-Functional Alignment: Partner seamlessly with Marketing, Risk, Credit, Compliance, Operations, and Platform teams, ensuring rigorous risk controls and establishing a clean handoff to the Retention team.
  • Address Funnel & Measurement Barriers: Establish robust funnel analytics to track new vs. existing user loan journeys separately, diagnosing and removing friction at every step.
  • Supervise AI Integration: Leverage AI tools with high accountability to accelerate product discovery, data analysis, and prototyping while establishing necessary guardrails and quality checks.


Requirements


  • Experience & Track Record: 7+ years of experience in product or growth management, with a proven track record leading high-velocity growth pods, ideally within fintech with a direct focus on consumer lending, credit products, or user acquisition/activation.
  • Fintech Experience: Proven track record as a Product Manager or growth manager, ideally within fintech with a focus on consumer lending, credit products, or high-velocity growth pods.
  • Growth & Experimentation Mastery: Demonstrated expertise in building acquisition and activation loops, running structured A/B tests, and leveraging funnel, cohort, and unit-economic analyses to drive scalable growth.
  • Product Discovery & Delivery: Hands-on experience identifying core user friction, defining crisp product solutions, prioritizing scope, and leading an agile squad to ship and iterate fast.
  • Bilingual Proficiency: Fluent in English; Spanish is a nice-to-have. Ability to communicate concisely, align cross-functional teams, and write clear product documentation.
  • High Agency & Extreme Ownership: Self-driven leader who proactively seeks missing information, removes blockers, and moves projects forward with minimal supervision.
  • Sound Judgment & Systems Thinking: Strong ability to structure ambiguous problems, make sound decisions under uncertainty, and anticipate downstream effects across user incentives, risk constraints, and financial mechanics.
  • AI Supervision & Quality Control: Proficiency in utilizing AI-assisted workflows to accelerate analysis while maintaining rigorous quality control over critical outputs.
  • These are the applicable requirements, although equivalent competencies in any of the above will also be considered.

What We Offer


  • Competitive salary
  • Initial stock options grant
  • Annual performance bonus
  • Health, dental, and vision plans
  • Remote work environment, although we have offices in Miami and México City and would love to work in hybrid model if you are up to it.
  • Continuous learning opportunities
  • Unlimited PTO
  • Paid parental leave
  • Empowering opportunities for growth in a dynamic entrepreneurial environment

Equal Opportunity Employer


At Félix, we are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all qualified employees and applicants without regard to race, religion, nationality, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, or disability. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruitment, hiring, placement, promotion, training, compensation, benefits, and termination.

Want to learn more about our privacy practices? Check out our Privacy Policy.

title: Field Technician 1
description:
WHAT WE DO

As a premier provider of environmental services in the Western United States, Patriot Environmental Services provides a wide range of industrial, emergency response and remediation services. We are committed to the principles of safety, superior customer service and experience, and unyielding quality and dedication.

We provide a broad array of environmental services to meet any need that our clients may have. From emergency spill response to hazardous waste transportation to wastewater treatment, or from industrial cleaning to full facility closure and remediation, Patriot can do it all with our own internal resources and do so while accomplishing every metric of success.

Our mission is to always be Prepared and Professional.

Join the team that makes a difference!

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Ensure that Health and Safety is the number one priority by complying with all safe work practices, policies, processes, and acting in a safe manner.
  • Perform emergency response cleanup activities including but not limited to chemical and water spills, non-hazardous and hazardous waste and toxic materials and equipment decontamination.
  • Sweep, dig, shovel, lift, pressure wash and handling drums to assist in cleanup.
  • Operate cleanup equipment used in hazardous waste activities.
  • Follow policies and procedures for control and storage of hazardous substances.
  • Attend safety training as required.
  • Comply with the Random Drug Testing Program.
  • Perform various housekeeping and custodial duties and other duties as required.
  • Assist with maintenance of facility like unloading trucks and other ancillary duties.
  • Answer 24/7 Emergency Response calls when on uncontrolled standby.
  • Work long hours and overtime during day, night or weekend shifts.
  • Other reasonable directives, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.

EXPERIENCE, EDUCATION AND REQUIREMENTS

  • High school diploma or GED preferred.
  • Some environmental services industry experience preferred.
  • Some hazardous waste control experience preferred.
  • Valid driver’s license required.
  • Driving record that meets company standards and current DMV printout, required.
  • 40-hour HAZWOPER certification required.
  • Confined Space Entry certification preferred.

SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES

  • Strong attention to detail; meticulous.
  • Safety conscious.
  • Patient
  • Flexible to fast paced changes.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS

  • Pushing / pulling: frequent daily basis
  • Twisting / turning: frequent daily basis
  • Lift items over head: frequent daily basis
  • Standing: 6-8 hours daily
  • Crouching / stooping: prolonged periods
  • Lifting / carrying: frequent daily up to 50 lbs
  • Work in confined spaces or at heights.
  • Required to wear a variety of personal protection equipment as required including but not limited to Tyvek suits.
  • Required to wear respirators as needed.
  • Performs labor intensive activities in all weather conditions during any hours during the day or night.

BENEFITS

  • PTO, paid holidays, sick time
  • Medical, dental, vision, life insurances
  • 401(k) with company matching

Pay: $18 - $25 per hour

Patriot Environmental Services is an equal opportunity employer (EOE)

title: Team Lead Dating Media Buying
description:

Join a fast-growing, international performance marketing environment where data-driven strategies and profitable growth are at the heart of the business. As Team Lead Dating Media Buying, you will combine hands-on campaign management with strategic ownership and people leadership. You will oversee high-budget campaigns across multiple traffic sources, markets, and verticals, driving revenue and return on investment. You will also mentor and develop a team of media buyers while building scalable processes and improving operational efficiency. Working closely with Business Intelligence, Product, Creative, and external partners, you will identify new opportunities and strengthen campaign performance. This is an opportunity to make a measurable business impact, influence growth strategy, and build a high-performing team in a dynamic, remote-first setting.

Accountabilities:

As Team Lead Dating Media Buying, you will own campaign performance, develop growth strategies, and lead a team responsible for scaling profitable acquisition activities. Your key responsibilities will include:

  • Campaign management and performance: Own, launch, optimize, and scale high-budget campaigns across multiple traffic sources, geographies, and verticals. Monitor performance metrics, report on results, and ensure revenue and ROI targets are achieved.

  • Growth strategy and experimentation: Develop and implement media buying strategies aligned with business objectives. Test new campaigns, funnels, creative angles, traffic sources, and markets while identifying scaling opportunities and performance inefficiencies.

  • Data-driven optimization: Use performance data, trends, and analytical insights to guide decisions, improve campaign outcomes, and establish a culture of continuous experimentation.

  • Partnerships and commercial development: Build relationships with advertising partners, networks, and sales representatives. Negotiate favorable deals, secure exclusive opportunities, improve margins, and identify new business and revenue streams.

  • Team leadership and development: Lead, mentor, and develop media buyers. Establish clear KPIs, performance expectations, and accountability standards while supporting recruitment, onboarding, and training.

  • Process and operational excellence: Improve workflows, campaign structures, and internal processes to support efficient, scalable operations across campaigns and teams.

  • Cross-functional collaboration: Work closely with Business Intelligence, Product, and Creative teams to maximize campaign effectiveness and align execution with broader growth priorities.

  • Industry awareness: Stay informed about advertising platform changes, emerging tools, traffic sources, and performance marketing trends to maintain a competitive advantage.

    The ideal candidate is a commercially minded performance marketing professional with a strong record of scaling profitable campaigns and the leadership skills to turn strategy into measurable results. You combine analytical rigor with a hands-on approach, take ownership of business outcomes, and thrive in a fast-paced environment. The key requirements include:

    • Professional experience: 4–6 or more years of experience in media buying or performance marketing.

    • Campaign performance: Demonstrated success managing high-spend campaigns profitably, working with substantial budgets, and implementing effective scaling strategies.

    • Analytical expertise: Strong understanding of performance data, campaign metrics, and ROI-driven optimization.

    • Ownership and decision-making: A strong sense of accountability for team and business results, with the ability to make sound decisions under uncertainty and prioritize effectively.

    • Communication and collaboration: Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to build productive relationships with internal teams and external partners.

    • Organization and discipline: A structured, proactive, and results-oriented approach to managing campaigns, budgets, and operational priorities.

    • Language proficiency: Fluent English, both written and spoken.

    • Affiliate marketing: Experience in affiliate marketing is an advantage.

    • Traffic sources: Familiarity with multiple advertising channels, such as Meta, native advertising, and display.

    • Advertising models: Strong understanding of CPM, CPC, CPL, and CPA pricing models.

    • Tools and tracking: Experience with Business Intelligence tools, tracking systems, or custom performance dashboards is beneficial.

      • Fully remote work environment with an international team.

description:
Who Are We?

FDH Aero is a trusted global supply chain partner for aerospace and defense companies, providing end-to-end supply chain solutions for OEM and aftermarket customers.

With more than 55+ years of experience and operations in 14 countries, we bring expertise across Commercial, Defense, Space, Business Aviation and Cargo through our specialized business divisions, Electronics, Hardware, Commercial Aftermarket, and Defense Aftermarket.

For more information, please visit the FDH Aero website.

Why Work Here?

Fast-paced & Impactful Work – Every decision helps keep aircraft flying and missions moving

Driven Team & Culture – Supportive, driven colleagues who support you every step of the way

High-Growth Opportunities – We invest in your success with training and development

Competitive Benefits Package – Includes medical, dental, vision insurance, Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) 401k matching, wellness activities and more

At FDH Aero, we understand that the strength of our brand comes from our people, and our culture empowers every team member to contribute and grow. As a global team, our culture is rooted in five (5) core values that begin with the words “We are” and include: service-first, respectful, amplifiers, open-minded and accountable.

We Are Looking For

The Order Verification Associate is responsible for ensuring order accuracy and inventory integrity. This role supports the fulfillment process by verifying customer orders against inventory records under close supervision, preparing materials for shipment, and conducting basic quality checks. This role serves as a key check and balance measure to prevent errors and ensure customer satisfaction.

What You’ll Do

As an Order Verification Associate, you’ll be responsible for:

  • Review and verify outgoing orders against customer purchase orders and internal documentation.
  • Ensure all items, quantities, and packaging meet company and customer requirements.
  • Identify and report discrepancies, such as incorrect items, quantities, or labeling issues, before shipment.
  • Collaborate with warehouse pickers, packers, and shipping teams to resolve order discrepancies.
  • Conduct quality checks on packaging, labeling, and documentation for compliance.
  • Utilize warehouse management systems (WMS) or other tracking tools to confirm order accuracy.
  • Maintain accurate records of verified orders and discrepancies for reporting purposes.
  • Follow all safety protocols and warehouse procedures to maintain a secure work environment.
  • Assist in process improvement initiatives to enhance accuracy and efficiency.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • No prior experience required; on-the-job training provided.
  • Eager to learn and follow instructions with strong attention to detail
  • Ability to work effectively as part of a team in a structured environment
  • Basic verbal communication skills to report issues and follow directives
  • Willingness to adhere to safety protocols and standard operating procedures under supervision

Special Requirements:

  • U.S. Citizen, U.S. Permanent Resident (Green Card holder) or asylee/refugee status as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) required.
  • ITAR Requirement
  • 120.15. Some positions will require current U.S. Citizenship due to contract requirements.

This position requires access to information that is subject to compliance with the International Traffic Arms Regulations (“ITAR”) and/or the Export Administration Regulations (“EAR”). In order to comply with the requirements of the ITAR and/or the EAR, applicants will be asked to provide specific documentation to verify U.S. person status under the ITAR and the EAR. A “U.S. person” according to their definition is a U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident (green card holder), or protected individual such as a refugee, or asylee. See 22 CFR

Job Type: Full Time

FDH Aero is an Equal Opportunity Employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Product Engineering Manager
description:
Mantel is developing the first molten-salt-based carbon capture technology designed to operate at the high temperatures found inside boilers, kilns, and furnaces, enabling highly efficient carbon capture that has not been possible until now. Carbon capture can be applied across industries to reduce emissions and achieve net-negative emissions. By solving for efficiency Mantel can cut costs substantially, unlocking carbon capture’s role in reaching net zero emissions by 2050. To learn more, go to:

The Product Engineering Manager role is about owning the equipment that makes Mantel’s technology work and is a key value driver of Mantel’s Licensing Business model. You’ll take our proprietary equipment packages (PEPs) from specification to delivery: picking the right vendors, holding them to the right standard, and making sure what arrives on site performs the way our process needs it to. This is part engineer, part project manager, and fully accountable for the outcome.

You’ll sit on the Product team and work at the intersections of engineering, projects and business development. When someone asks “where are we on that equipment?”, you’re the person with the answer. This is a role as a technical manager working to deliver through a commercial lens. You don’t need to have all the technical answers, but you should be technical enough to know who or what to ask.

This is initially an individual contributor role with high visibility. You’ll work closely with senior leadership and own your packages end to end from day one. Expect to travel to vendor shops and project sites up to 25% of the time.

What you’ll do:

1. Equipment Package Ownership

  • Develop Mantel’s PEPs alongside internal and external engineering resources, defining scope, battery limits, and how our equipment integrates with the broader plant design

  • Own the technical and commercial scope for Mantel’s PEPs across projects

  • Be the single point of accountability for each package, from first spec to installed and running

  • Translate process requirements into clear specifications, datasheets, and scopes of supply for Mantel’s projects

2. Vendor Selection & Management

  • Find, qualify, and select the vendors and fabricators who can build first-of-a-kind equipment well

  • Run RFQs and bid evaluations; compare vendors on technical capability, cost, schedule, and quality, not just price

  • Manage vendors through design, fabrication, inspection, and delivery, and push back when something isn’t right

  • Protect Mantel’s intellectual property in every vendor engagement

3. Project Engineering

  • Lead design reviews and drawing approvals, and manage the interfaces between our equipment and the rest of the plant

  • Keep vendor documentation, technical queries, and changes organized and moving

  • Coordinate shop inspections and factory acceptance testing, and make sure the quality paperwork is complete

4. Project Management

  • Build and manage schedules and budgets for each package

  • Track progress, flag risks early, and drive issues to resolution rather than reporting on them

  • Manage change orders with a clear view of cost and schedule impact

5. Delivery, Commissioning & Continuous Improvement

  • Support installation and commissioning alongside our field teams and help resolve equipment issues on site

  • Capture what we learn on each project and feed it back into design standards, vendor strategy, and the next generation of equipment

Who You Are:

  • Experience: 7+ years in project engineering, equipment engineering, or package management for process or industrial facilities

  • Education: B.S. in Mechanical or Chemical/Process Engineering required

Put differently,

  • You’ve taken equipment from a spec sheet to a running plant, and you know where it usually goes wrong

  • You can read a P&ID and a GA drawing, and you can tell when a vendor is overpromising

  • You’re equally comfortable in a design review and on a fabrication shop floor

  • You keep schedules, budgets, and paperwork under control without letting them become the job

  • You hold vendors accountable firmly but fairly, and they still want to work with you

  • You like first-of-a-kind problems more than repeating what’s been done before

  • You’re low-ego, direct, and you follow through

What You’ll Get:

  • Ownership of the equipment at the heart of Mantel’s technology, at the moment we move from demonstration to commercial deployment

  • A role that shapes our vendor base, design standards, and how Mantel builds equipment for years to come

  • Close collaboration with senior leadership and a growing scope as Mantel scales

  • A central role in building one of the most exciting carbon capture companies in the world

We provide competitive and holistic compensation to all our full-time team members, including:

  • Highly competitive pay based on experience, including equity

  • 90% subsidized medical and dental healthcare coverage for employees, 50% for dependents

  • Unlimited vacation policy, mental health personal days, generous sick leave, plus a week-long winter break at the end of December

  • Health/Fitness and cell phone stipend

  • Paid parental leave

title: Visiting Instructor - Biology
description:

The Niagara University College of Arts and Sciences Department of Biology is seeking outstanding Visiting Laboratory Microbiology Instructor candidates. The Laboratory Instructor will be responsible for teaching microbiology with laboratory courses in the Department of Biology for both biology and nursing majors. We seek applicants with an interest in fostering rigorous, inclusive, and high-impact learning environments. Candidates of diverse backgrounds are encouraged to apply. The position will be Spring Semester 2027, from January until May. Submit cover letter, C.V., and three references along with a statement of teaching philosophy through the application portal.

  • A Master's degree or higher in Medical Microbiology and/or Biomedical sciences or related field.
  • Demonstrated experience in microbiological techniques.
  • Teaching experience at the university level.
  • Candidates should demonstrate knowledge of and the ability to use technology to support instruction.
  • An understanding and commitment to working with faculty, staff, and students from diverse cultures and backgrounds.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Doctorate in Medical Microbiology, Biomedical sciences and/or a related field.
  • Demonstrated ability to teach core courses in biology (e.g., microbiology, anatomy and physiology, introductory biology or capstone writing course).
  • In addition to a strong academic background, applicants with experience supporting research training for undergraduates are encouraged to apply.

title: Product Manager Privacy
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Product Manager Privacy based in Switzerland.

Take ownership of privacy and consent management across a suite of digital advertising products spanning web, mobile apps, and connected TV (CTV). In this strategic product role, you will lead the Privacy squad and report directly to the VP of Product, shaping how consent signals are collected, interpreted, and transmitted across multiple advertising channels. Your mission is to maximize publisher revenue while ensuring compliance with applicable privacy regulations and industry standards. You will translate complex legal frameworks into practical product specifications, balancing regulatory obligations with commercial opportunities. Working closely with engineering, analytics, UX, engagement teams, and privacy experts, you will drive measurable improvements in consent management and monetization. Join a fast-growing, international, AI-driven environment where analytical thinking, ownership, and pragmatic decision-making are central to success.

Accountabilities:

As Product Manager Privacy, you will own the consent management strategy, lead the Privacy squad, and ensure that privacy requirements are consistently implemented across products and channels. Your main responsibilities will include:

  • Consent Engine and Frameworks: Own the FastCMP consent signal engine roadmap, covering IAB TCF, GPP, Global Privacy Control (GPC), Google Consent Mode, and US privacy signals. Define the applicable frameworks and default behaviors for each jurisdiction, and deliver new standard versions on time across web, mobile, and CTV.

  • Cross-Product Privacy Rules: Translate legislation and industry standards into clear product specifications for Actirise, Viously, and Meetscale across web, app, and CTV. Maintain a compliance checklist for consent-related initiatives and coordinate with product managers to ensure signals are correctly collected, respected, and transmitted.

  • Privacy-Compliant Monetization: Identify opportunities to monetize traffic within applicable privacy rules. Distinguish mandatory requirements from recommendations, assess revenue implications before making decisions, and evaluate options for traffic with no or partial consent, including legitimate interest, contextual advertising, and no-ad requirements.

  • Measurement and Decision-Making: Apply a measure-before-deciding approach, ensuring traffic is not rejected or degraded without supporting measurements and a documented decision.

  • Compliance, Vendors, and Certifications: Own IAB TCF and Google CMP certifications, manage vendor lists and custom vendors, and mitigate the risk of deregistration. Work with the Data Protection Officer (DPO) to validate privacy interpretations while retaining product ownership of decisions.

  • Client and Partner Engagement: Serve as the product point of contact for strategic clients and partners on privacy matters, including CMP migrations, regulatory requests, and buyer requirements.

  • Regulatory and Standards Monitoring: Track upcoming legislation and industry standards, anticipate their product implications, and translate them into roadmap priorities before they become urgent.

  • AI-Ready Product Management: Apply an agentic-first approach by ensuring privacy rules and configurations can be executed by AI agents, supported by clean data contracts and appropriate access controls.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Engagement, UX Orchestration, Analytics, FastCMP engineering, and the DPO to coordinate consent templates, A/B testing, CMP and paywall configurations, and privacy signal measurement.

    • Requirements:

    The ideal candidate combines substantial privacy expertise with hands-on product management experience in advertising technology. You understand how to interpret legal requirements without unnecessarily restricting legitimate business opportunities, and you can translate complex rules into actionable technical specifications. The following qualifications are expected:

    • Privacy and Product Experience: At least 5 years of experience in privacy, consent management platforms (CMPs), or ad tech, including product management experience and a proven track record of shipping products in this ecosystem.

    • Industry Standards and Regulations: Strong knowledge of IAB TCF, Global Privacy Platform (GPP), OpenRTB consent fields, GDPR, ePrivacy, and US privacy legislation, including CCPA and applicable state laws.

    • Commercial and Analytical Judgment: Ability to distinguish legal obligations from recommendations and support product decisions with data, evidence, and measurable revenue impact.

    • Technical Specification Skills: Ability to write precise, implementation-ready specifications that engineers can execute with minimal clarification. Programming experience is not required.

    • Data-Driven Approach: Familiarity with basic SQL, dashboards, analytics, and A/B testing, with a commitment to measuring outcomes before making decisions.

    • AI and Agentic Workflows: Daily use of an AI assistant, such as Claude, and practical experience building AI-enabled skills or agentic workflows within product management.

    • Communication Skills: Fluent in both English and French, with the ability to communicate effectively with legal specialists, engineers, product teams, clients, and business stakeholders.

    • Problem-Solving Mindset: Pragmatic, analytical, and comfortable making decisions in a fast-moving environment. You understand the Pareto principle and know how to prioritize high-impact improvements.

    • Collaboration and Ownership: Strong listening skills, a willingness to challenge existing practices constructively, and a commitment to continuous improvement and shared team goals.

      • Benefits:

      • Fully Remote Work: Work remotely within a flexible environment, with access to offices in Paris, Lille, or London.

      • International Work Environment: Collaborate with colleagues across multiple countries, with English as the working language.

      • AI Tools: Access to Claude for everyday work and AI-enabled workflows.

      • Collaborative Culture: Join a close-knit, supportive team that values innovation, knowledge-sharing, and collective success.

      • Social Events: Participate in regular team gatherings and company events.

      • Career Development: Benefit from training programs, HR career check-ins, internal mobility opportunities, and regular performance feedback.

      • Health Coverage: Access to a comprehensive health insurance plan.

      • Growth Opportunities: Contribute to a rapidly expanding digital advertising technology environment and help shape the future of privacy-aware monetization.

      • Inclusive Workplace: Work in an environment committed to diversity, equal opportunities, and inclusion.

      • Employment Type: Full-time.

      • Recruitment Process: The process includes a screening call with Talent Acquisition, an interview with the VP of Product, a case study with the VP of Product and DPO, and reference checks. Interviews are primarily conducted by video conference, although some stages may require an in-person meeting.

title: Partner Solutions Engineer
description:
What You Can Expect


Zoom is seeking a Partner Solutions Engineer with strong Customer Experience (CX) and Contact Center experience to help partners grow their Zoom practice and deliver modern, AI-first customer engagement solutions.


In this role, you will work closely with channel partners across North America to enable, position, and expand Zoom Customer Experience solutions. You will act as a trusted technical advisor, helping partners connect business needs to practical solution designs across CX, AI, voice, and adjacent platform capabilities.


The ideal candidate brings deep CX knowledge, strong channel experience, technical credibility, and a passion for helping partners build differentiated solutions that improve customer engagement and business outcomes.

About the Team


Zoom helps people and businesses connect, collaborate, and deliver better experiences. As we continue to grow our partner ecosystem, the Partner Solutions Engineering team plays a critical role in helping partners build, position, and scale Zoom solutions in the market.

Responsibilities


  • Serve as a pre-sales technical advisor to channel partners across North America, with a focus on CX and contact center solutions.
  • Build strong relationships with partner pre-sales teams, architects, practice leaders, and other key stakeholders.
  • Lead technical onboarding and enablement for partners building or expanding Zoom Customer Experience capabilities.
  • Deliver technical workshops, training sessions, demos, and ongoing enablement aligned to partner maturity and growth goals.
  • Work with priority partners to build and execute technical plans that grow adoption, strengthen solution readiness, and expand their Zoom CX practice.
  • Translate partner business goals and technical requirements into scalable solution designs and recommended architectures.
  • Help partners position AI as a core part of modern CX transformation, including self-service, agent assist, analytics, automation, and customer engagement workflows.
  • Maintain working knowledge of adjacent Zoom portfolio areas, including voice, AI, and platform capabilities that support broader CX-led conversations.
  • Collaborate with internal sales, product, partner, and specialist teams to share field feedback, address adoption blockers, and improve partner readiness.
  • Understand and communicate relevant security, compliance, and regulatory considerations within CX and contact center environments.

What We're Looking For


  • 5+ years of solution engineering, sales engineering, partner engineering, or related experience in CX, CCaaS, or cloud contact center environments.
  • Strong knowledge of modern CX technologies and workflows, including contact center, workforce engagement, analytics, conversational AI, chatbots, voicebots, workflow automation, and customer journey solutions.
  • Experience working with channel partners on technical enablement, practice development, and solution strategy.
  • Ability to position CX solutions within broader communications, collaboration, and AI platform conversations.
  • Understanding of AI-driven trends shaping the CX and CCaaS market.
  • Experience building and executing partner technical enablement or growth plans.
  • Strong presentation, communication, and relationship-building skills.
  • Understanding of sell-through channel models and partner business structures.
  • Experience implementing, designing, or architecting CX solutions is a plus.


Salary Range or On Target Earnings:

$131,200.00 - $262,400.00

In addition to the base salary and/or OTE listed Zoom has a Total Direct Compensation philosophy that takes into consideration; base salary, bonus and equity value.

Note: Starting pay will be based on a number of factors and commensurate with qualifications & experience.


We also have a location based compensation structure; there may be a different range for candidates in this and other locations

11/22/26

Our structured hybrid approach is centered around our offices and remote work environments. The work style of each role, Hybrid, Remote, or In-Person is indicated in the job description/posting.


Benefits
As part of our award-winning workplace culture and commitment to delivering happiness, our benefits program offers a variety of perks, benefits, and options to help employees maintain their physical, mental, emotional, and financial health; support work-life balance; and contribute to their community in meaningful ways. Click Learnfor more information.

Zoomies help people stay connected so they can get more done together. We set out to build the best collaboration platform for the enterprise, and today help people communicate better with products like Zoom Contact Center, Zoom Phone, Zoom Events, Zoom Apps, Zoom Rooms, and Zoom Webinars.
We’re problem-solvers, working at a fast pace to design solutions with our customers and users in mind. Find room to grow with opportunities to stretch your skills and advance your career in a collaborative, growth-focused environment.

Our Commitment

title: Technical Project Manager II -IRT
description:
About YPrime:

At YPrime, we pioneer solutions that streamline the clinical trial journey, increasing certainty from study design to data lock. With a foundation built on decades of industry insight and expertise, we are inspired by the life-altering outcomes unlocked by clinical trials. Our dedication to quality is pivotal in propelling the groundbreaking endeavors of our partners, researchers, and investigators. With a technology platform that enables speed, flexibility, and certainty for large and emerging pharma companies alike, we provide eConsent, eCOA, IRT, and patient engagement solutions that solve with certainty in clinical research.


About the Role:

As a Technical Project Manager, you'll lead the design and delivery of IRT solutions for clinical trials. Partnering with sponsors and internal subject matter experts, you'll gather requirements, translate study protocols into system designs, and guide studies through build, testing, and launch. This is a highly consultative role that combines project leadership, solution design, and problem-solving. You'll help shape how each study operates within the IRT platform, ensuring solutions are scalable, effective, and aligned with trial objectives.


Responsibilities:

  • Ensure all requirements for system build are identified, documented, and communicated across the project team
  • Consistent implementation of Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC)
  • Responsible for the technical design of basic studies based on protocol, client requests and experience
  • Review and support configuration of basic systems; understand the capabilities of base product to ensure custom code is not created inadvertently
  • Ensures all functional requirements are captured in Systems Requirements Document (SRD) and other applicable system requirements documents
  • Group functionalities and requirements that are similar together, and approach the design holistically
  • Translates functional requirements into technical specifications for programmers
  • Leads team in ad-hoc testing of requirements in development environment
  • Ensures delivery of a clean study through validation environment
  • Objectively review and approve system documentation and specifications as required
  • Ensure documentation completeness and compliance of all YPrime SOPs and WIs
  • Support system validation through the timely triaging of defects
  • Demonstrates software prototypes for customers
  • Assist in mentoring configuration specialists, if applicable
  • Sets and tracks project milestones related to technical delivery; manages and accounts for unforeseen delays, then realigns schedules and expectations as needed.
  • Communicates and coordinates project milestones with internal team
  • Assist in mentoring more junior Technical Project Managers
  • Assist in project scoping and change control processes, including revision management
  • Adopts new processes and skills with minimal to no managerial oversight
  • Responsible for the technical design of intermediate studies and system changes based on protocol, client requests and experience
  • Review and support configuration of intermediate systems
  • Research defect record frequency by type and proposes methods to reduce defect records, if applicable
  • Works independently with YPrime team members to rectify UAT issues
  • Work with cross-functional groups at YPrime to help develop, implement and document standards
  • Uses past experiences and advanced knowledge of the system to strategically plan and mitigate risk
  • Support audit preparation and activities as expected
  • Perform other related duties as required


Skills:

  • Comfort working with IRT
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Exceptional focus on detail
  • Time management and organizational skills
  • Creative problem-solving ability
  • Sense of ownership and proactivity


Education & Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent experience, preferred
  • Proficient in MS Office applications required, database querying experience preferred (SQL Server)
  • Foundational knowledge of the principles of SDLC required
  • Experience in biotech/pharmaceutical or the CRO industry preferred
  • Experience with Scrum Software Development is considered a plus
  • Experience with SaaS delivery is considered a plus
  • Technical management experience a plus
  • Experience with software systems in support of clinical trials
  • Experience in IRT is required

title: Director, Digital Experience and Engagement
description:
Director, Digital Experience and Engagement

D30: $130,000 – $135,000

Learning, Innovation, and Technology Solutions (LITS)

102 West State Street Trenton, NJ 08608


Thomas Edison State University was founded in 1972 to break down barriers to degree completion. Fifty years later, it proudly serves a diverse body of adult students with innovative and professionally relevant academic programming in a predominantly online delivery. Our team of high-energy student-focused professionals is welcoming new members who are making their mark in education and are ready to help change the lives of thousands of adult students across New Jersey and around the world.


Candidates who are excited by changing lives, committed to the success of all and want to be challenged by new and innovative opportunities, should submit an application.

Summary:


The Director, Digital Experience and Engagement provides strategic and operational leadership for the University’s digital engagement ecosystem. The director is accountable for the portfolio of platforms that enable coordinated, accessible, secure, and audience-centered interaction across recruitment, enrollment, learning, student support, employee services, completion, alumni engagement, and other University relationships.


The University’s customer relationship management system is the role’s immediate anchor platform, but not its organizational boundary. The portfolio is expected to include the student portal and may expand to enterprise email and text messaging, notifications, chat and conversational services, knowledge tools, appointment and form technologies, communication preference management, and responsible AI-enabled engagement capabilities.


The director works primarily with University departments and service owners to translate institutional goals, audience needs, and business processes into a coherent technology roadmap. The role convenes partners across LITS, Admissions, University Communications, Student Success, Academic Affairs, schools, and other units. It owns enabling platforms, channel architecture, technical governance, product roadmaps, and service outcomes; it does not replace the institutional voice, brand, editorial, or campaign ownership of University Communications and functional offices.

Leadership Scope:

- Establish Digital Experience and Engagement as a collaborative, enterprise-facing function rather than a single-product administration team.

- Serve as LITS product and portfolio owner for assigned engagement platforms, with authority to recommend standards, consolidation, investment, lifecycle decisions, and operating models.

- Develop internal platform expertise during the Element451 implementation in partnership with the named University implementation lead and prepare LITS for sustainable technical stewardship after implementation.

- Provide enough technical depth to guide architecture, integration, configuration, privacy, security, and vendor decisions while coordinating hands-on engineering with the appropriate LITS teams and vendors.

- Build a high-trust operating model in which ownership is clear, delivery is shared, and cross-functional partners are engaged early.


Essential Responsibility Areas:

Portfolio strategy and governance

- Develop and maintain a University-wide roadmap for assigned digital experience and engagement capabilities, linking investment decisions to institutional priorities and audience outcomes.

- Inventory and rationalize engagement platforms; clarify the intended purpose, audience, lifecycle, owner, and integration pattern for each channel and product.

- Establish standards for platform selection, configuration, channel use, permissions, accessibility, privacy, records, communication preferences, automation, AI, and lifecycle management.

- Convene a cross-functional governance structure that defines decision rights without displacing the content, policy, or business-process authority of partner offices.


CRM and engagement platform stewardship

- Partner with the University’s named Element451 implementation lead to build LITS platform knowledge, document the operating model, and prepare for long-term technical stewardship.

- Own assigned platform roadmaps, configuration standards, release planning, administrative practices, service levels, vendor relationships, and support escalation models.

- Translate functional needs into prioritized platform requirements and coordinate integration, identity, security, data, and infrastructure work with Enterprise Business Systems, Enterprise Technologies, Data & Analytics, and vendors.

- Ensure that roles, environments, documentation, testing, change controls, recovery plans, and knowledge transfer support reliable operations.


Digital experience and portal leadership

- Lead the authenticated portal as an enterprise digital front door, with clear product ownership, roadmap, governance, and measures of usefulness.

- Organize experiences around audience needs, tasks, and lifecycle moments rather than University organizational boundaries.

- Coordinate content, alerts, transactions, search, personalization, accessibility, and integration with University Communications, functional offices, web leadership, and LITS platform owners.

- Use research, service data, and feedback to identify friction and prioritize improvements across student, employee, mentor/faculty, and other University experiences.


Cross-functional service and journey enablement

- Help departments map audience journeys, communication needs, interventions, and handoffs, and then apply enterprise platforms to support them.

- Facilitate shared design decisions among Admissions, University Communications, schools, student services, academic and administrative offices, and LITS teams.

- Define escalation paths and coordination practices for urgent, sensitive, high-impact, or cross-channel communications.

- Promote reusable patterns, templates, and communities of practice so departments can collaborate freely while maintaining enterprise standards.


Platform operations, vendors, and resources

- Develop annual plans, budgets, staffing recommendations, contract strategies, service expectations, and lifecycle plans for the portfolio.

- Lead assigned staff and coordinate matrixed project teams, consultants, and vendors; set clear priorities and follow-through expectations.

- Manage platform risks, incidents, maintenance, adoption, technical debt, and vendor performance in collaboration with security, infrastructure, application, data, and service teams.

- Maintain decision records, platform documentation, ownership maps, and practical support knowledge.


Measurement, adoption, and continuous improvement

- Define outcomes and measures for reach, engagement, task completion, service adoption, satisfaction, reliability, accessibility, and platform value.

- Work with Data & Analytics and functional partners to create appropriate dashboards and insight loops without duplicating institutional analytics ownership.

- Lead adoption and change-enablement efforts for new or improved platforms, including communication, training, documentation, and stakeholder readiness.

- Use evidence to prioritize improvements, retire low-value tools, and reduce fragmented or contradictory digital experiences.


People and organizational leadership

CIVIC and Human Rights Activists in Iran (HRA) are undertaking communications and advocacy campaign to amplify awareness of the human costs of the US war in Iran by telling compelling, human-centered stories about civilian harm.

Project Description & Scope of Work: To support the development of content amplifying these stories, CIVIC is seeking to recruit a Multimedia Production and Content Creation Consultant. The consultant will work closely with CIVIC and HRA to design documented testimonies, evidence, and advocacy messages into engaging visual and multimedia content for public dissemination. This will include the production of professional, high-resolution videos suitable for social media platforms, as well as graphics, carousel, and animated videos as required.

Based on documentation collected and curated by HRA, the consultant will collaborate with CIVIC to develop a creative storytelling approach, including visual style, format selection, and audience engagement strategies. The consultant will spearhead the production process, including visual design, video editing, motion graphics, subtitling, sound design, integration of photographs, video footage, interviews, and other source materials as relevant. The consultant will also consult on storyboarding and script development.

All products must adhere to conflict-sensitive and trauma-informed communications principles, ensuring that storytelling approaches do not expose contributors, affected communities, or partners to undue risk. The consultant will work iteratively with CIVIC and HRA throughout the process, incorporating feedback and revisions to ensure that final products align with project objectives, advocacy priorities, and ethical storytelling standards.

The consultant must preserve the factual and contextual integrity of testimonies and source materials. Any substantive editing, reconstruction, use of generative AI, synthetic imagery or audio, or alteration of documentary materials must receive prior written approval from CIVIC and must not misrepresent the experiences or statements of contributors.

Where publication may create protection, privacy, or security risks, the consultant should work with CIVIC and HRA to apply appropriate mitigation measures, including anonymization, blurring, voice alteration, removal of identifying information or metadata, and secure handling and transfer of source files.

Under the supervision of the US Director, the consultant will undertake the following activities:

  • Develop compelling multimedia content (including graphics and videos) amplifying the experiences of Iranian civilians during the US-Israel-Iran war;
  • Consult with the CIVIC and HRA teams on storyboarding and script development;
  • Brainstorm innovative concepts to shape raw materials from the ground into engaging, high-impact content.
  • Produce and deliver edited videos (approximately 1-3 minutes in length) adapted to the formats agreed upon by the CIVIC and HRA teams and the consultant;
  • Edit photos (selection and color correction) and videos (editing, color correction, color integration and subtitles);
  • Propose creative formats tailored for various platforms, ensuring all outputs strictly align with CIVIC’s tone of voice and branding.
  • Ensure that the free and informed consent of the persons filmed or photographed is obtained and properly archived internally, and that CIVIC's principles of confidentiality, data protection and ethics are strictly adhered to;
  • Ensure compliance with the visibility and visual identity requirements of CIVIC; and
  • Consult with CIVIC and HRA teams in the design and implementation of a tailored dissemination strategy.

Deliverables

  • A set of edited high-resolution graphics (3-5) and 30-90 second 3-4 videos (exact number and format to be agreed upon with CIVIC and HRA teams); ready for use on digital platforms, including social media, presentations and donor reports;
  • Raw files (photos and videos) to be sent to the designated focal point and properly archived in line with CIVIC's standard;
  • Complete captions and corresponding contextual notes; and
  • Signed consent forms, where required.

Duration and terms

  • Duration: 3 months (subject to extension based on delivery timeline)
  • Level of effort: Varied, as required
  • Location: Remote
    from United States, the Netherlands, Belgium, or Kenya, with work authorization in operating location, a commitment to align with US team time zones when needed, and stable internet connection for video calls and transferring large files.

Qualifications and experience

    • Minimum three (3) years of professional experience in photography and videography, graphic design, social media content creation, and/or communications;
    • Strong command of video and photo editing software, including the Adobe Creative Cloud suite (Premiere Pro, After Effects, Audition, Lightroom, and Photoshop).
    • Proven experience working with non-profits or on development and/or humanitarian projects;
    • Strong portfolio demonstrating relevant work, particularly in humanitarian and sensitive contexts;
    • Strong knowledge of ethical storytelling practices, informed consent and protection principles;
    • Ability to work in sensitive and conflict-affected environments; and
    • Fluency in English; knowledge of Farsi is an asset.
  • Intellectual property and confidentiality: All materials produced as part of this consultancy will be the exclusive property of CIVIC. Any use of the materials for personal purposes (including in a portfolio) will require prior written authorization from CIVIC. The consultant must strictly comply with the confidentiality, backup, and data protection requirements applicable throughout the duration of the assignment.
  • Equipment: The consultant must have their own professional equipment (e.g., camera, audio equipment, and editing and graphic design software (Adobe Creative Cloud suite).

Payment terms

Take ownership of privacy and consent management across a suite of digital advertising products spanning web, mobile apps, and connected TV (CTV). In this strategic product role, you will lead the Privacy squad and report directly to the VP of Product, shaping how consent signals are collected, interpreted, and transmitted across multiple advertising channels. Your mission is to maximize publisher revenue while ensuring compliance with applicable privacy regulations and industry standards. You will translate complex legal frameworks into practical product specifications, balancing regulatory obligations with commercial opportunities. Working closely with engineering, analytics, UX, engagement teams, and privacy experts, you will drive measurable improvements in consent management and monetization. Join a fast-growing, international, AI-driven environment where analytical thinking, ownership, and pragmatic decision-making are central to success.

Accountabilities:

  • Consent Engine and Frameworks: Own the FastCMP consent signal engine roadmap, covering IAB TCF, GPP, Global Privacy Control (GPC), Google Consent Mode, and US privacy signals. Define the applicable frameworks and default behaviors for each jurisdiction, and deliver new standard versions on time across web, mobile, and CTV.

  • Cross-Product Privacy Rules: Translate legislation and industry standards into clear product specifications for Actirise, Viously, and Meetscale across web, app, and CTV. Maintain a compliance checklist for consent-related initiatives and coordinate with product managers to ensure signals are correctly collected, respected, and transmitted.

  • Privacy-Compliant Monetization: Identify opportunities to monetize traffic within applicable privacy rules. Distinguish mandatory requirements from recommendations, assess revenue implications before making decisions, and evaluate options for traffic with no or partial consent, including legitimate interest, contextual advertising, and no-ad requirements.

  • Measurement and Decision-Making: Apply a measure-before-deciding approach, ensuring traffic is not rejected or degraded without supporting measurements and a documented decision.

  • Compliance, Vendors, and Certifications: Own IAB TCF and Google CMP certifications, manage vendor lists and custom vendors, and mitigate the risk of deregistration. Work with the Data Protection Officer (DPO) to validate privacy interpretations while retaining product ownership of decisions.

The role ensures raw materials, in‑process controls, finished goods, and hygiene/sanitation meet internal specs, customer expectations, and regulatory/third‑party standards. Quality Improvement

  • Lead quality improvement projects with Operations using scientific, data-driven problem solving.

People Leadership & Development

title: Weights and Measures Specialist
description:
Position Summary

The Weights & Measures (W&M) Specialist is responsible for the end-to-end execution of the W&M process: getting meters to county W&M offices for testing, securing their release, and moving tested meters to our central warehouse or directly to the customer site. This position ensures that every W&M order moves on time and that every movement is recorded correctly in NetSuite, so that inventory stays accurate at every step.

This role is the primary point of contact for county W&M offices and for clients with questions about W&M orders. It coordinates between internal teams and external partners, and serves as a cross-trained backup to the Supply Chain Specialists.

Core Responsibilities

  1. County Coordination & Release
  • County Communication: Serve as the primary contact for county W&M offices on testing status, release permissions, pickup windows, and failed or missing meters. Follow up until every open order is resolved.
  • Release Management: Request the release of tested meters and track every order through the county release queue, so tested meters do not sit at the county after testing is complete.
  • Stakeholder Coordination: Coordinate between internal stakeholders (Scheduling, Customer Support, Field Operations, Inventory Control, and the central warehouse) and external partners (counties, couriers, carriers, and the 3PL) so everyone works from the same dates.
  • Failed Meter Resolution: Coordinate the return, replacement, or retest of meters that fail county testing.
  1. W&M Shipments & Logistics
  • Shipments to Counties: Prepare and request shipments of meters to county W&M offices for testing, including any required approvals, and update the W&M status on each order as it moves through every step of the process.
  • Courier & Freight Booking: Book the couriers and freight needed to move equipment to and from county W&M offices, mostly pickups from the county. The central warehouse books its own freight for the shipments it sends.
  • County to Central Warehouse: Coordinate shipments of tested meters from the county to the central warehouse: schedule pickups with the county and courier, and confirm receipt at the warehouse.
  • County Direct to Customer: Coordinate direct delivery of tested meters from the county to the customer site: confirm delivery details with the property, schedule the county and courier, and confirm delivery on arrival.
  • Partial Deliveries: When a delivery is short, record what arrived and track the balance until it is delivered.
  • Tracking & Transparency: Enter tracking and delivery details for every W&M shipment in NetSuite.
  1. Transaction Accuracy
  • Transaction Ownership: Create every W&M transaction in NetSuite accurately and on the same day the movement happens: transfer orders to and from county locations, item fulfillments, and receipts. No physical movement goes unrecorded.
  • Assembly Builds: Create the assembly builds that convert untested meters into tested meters once the county passes them, making sure the quantity built matches the components consumed and the quantity the county passed.
  • Status Accuracy: Keep the W&M status on every sales order current at each step, so that the order status always reflects where the meters physically are.
  • Lot & Quantity Accuracy: Record lot numbers and quantities correctly the first time on every transaction, matching tested and failed quantities to what the county reports.
  • Daily Movement Check: Confirm each day that every physical W&M movement has a matching NetSuite transaction, and report any gap to Inventory Control the same day.
  • Inventory Control Support: Support cycle counts and variance research when Inventory Control asks. Inventory Control owns reconciliation, cycle counts, and all corrections and adjustments; this role owns getting each transaction right the first time.
  • SOP Adherence: Follow documented Standard Operating Procedures and transaction checklists, and keep the checklists current.

  • Zendesk Client Support: Respond directly to client inquiries in Zendesk about W&M orders, including testing status, release timing, shipment tracking, and delivery dates. Provide accurate, timely responses and escalate unresolved issues to the appropriate team.

title: Team Lead Dating Media Buying

title: Deputy Director of School-Year Programs
description:
DEPUTY DIRECTOR OF SCHOOL-YEAR PROGRAMS (FULL-TIME)


Since 1877, The Fresh Air Fund (Fresh Air) has been a leading youth development organization providing transformative opportunities for children and young adults from New York City's underserved communities. Rooted in the belief that access to nature and outdoor experiences can change lives, Fresh Air connects young people to the outdoors while providing opportunities for personal growth, leadership development and exploration. Through free summer camp and year-round leadership development, educational enrichment and career exploration programs, Fresh Air helps young people develop the skills, confidence and connections they need to thrive.


Serving more than 1.8 million children throughout its history, Fresh Air remains committed to expanding access to life-changing experiences that empower young people to reach their full potential. At Fresh Air, employees are driven by purpose, collaboration and a shared commitment to creating opportunities that help young people succeed.

Position Summary

The Deputy Director of School-Year Programs partners closely with the Director of School-Year Programs to plan, implement, supervise, and continuously improve Fresh Air’s school-year program portfolio. As a key member of the School-Year Programs leadership team, the Deputy Director shares responsibility for program quality, youth safety, staff development, participant engagement, and consistent delivery of engaging, youth-centered experiences that connect young people with nature and the outdoors.


Reporting to the Director of School-Year Programs, the Deputy Director takes a hands-on leadership role in day-to-day program operations, including staffing, schedules, curriculum and lesson planning, training, on-site facilitation, logistics, and troubleshooting. The Deputy Director works collaboratively with the Director on priorities and decisions, independently manages delegated operational responsibilities, and keeps the Director informed of progress, risks, and emerging needs.


Responsibilities

Collaborative Leadership and Program Planning

  • Partner with the Director to translate department-wide goals, priorities, and youth development outcomes into actionable program plans, schedules, milestones, and team expectations.
  • Participate actively in program design, implementation, evaluation, and improvement; bring operational insights, staff feedback, and youth and family perspectives into shared planning and decision-making.
  • Coordinate across school-year programs and Camping teams to strengthen consistency, outdoor learning opportunities, and connections between summer and school-year experiences.
  • Provide clear, timely updates to the Director on program readiness, staffing, risks, results, and decisions requiring escalation.

Day-to-Day Program Operations and On-Site Leadership

  • Lead daily coordination of school-year programming, including calendars, staffing coverage, session preparation, transportation, supplies, vendors, facilities, and activity logistics.
  • Ensure program coordinators and frontline staff have clear work plans, session agendas, materials, participant information, and contingency plans before each program.
  • Provide direct on-site leadership during scheduled programs, including evenings and Saturdays; facilitate activities, support staff, and respond to operational needs in real time.
  • Monitor attendance, enrollment, participant retention, and family communications; identify gaps and coordinate timely follow-up with staff and relevant departments.
  • Implement established safety procedures, incident response and escalation protocols, and program policies; promptly communicate significant concerns to the Director.
  • Coordinate program-related support for camp departures and returns and other cross-program activities as assigned.

Curriculum Design, Facilitation, and Program Quality

  • Develop, adapt, and review age-appropriate curricula, session plans, and hands-on activities grounded in youth development, social-emotional learning, leadership, and outdoor exploration.
  • Directly facilitate youth sessions, group discussions, staff workshops, orientations, and other learning experiences as needed; model engaging and inclusive facilitation techniques.
  • Coach program coordinators and facilitators on lesson design, group management, experiential learning, and adapting activities for diverse participant needs.
  • Conduct program observations and debriefs with staff, using feedback and evaluation findings to improve instructional quality and participant experience.
  • Work with the Director and Camping partners to align school-year curriculum with broader Fresh Air programming goals.

Staff and Volunteer Supervision and Development

  • Directly supervise assigned program coordinators and part-time staff, with clear work expectations, regular check-ins, coaching, performance feedback, and accountability for deliverables.
  • Partner with the Director on staffing plans, recruitment, interviews, hiring recommendations, onboarding, training, scheduling, and retention.
  • Coordinate and facilitate staff and volunteer orientations and ongoing professional development, emphasizing youth safety, inclusive practices, and effective facilitation.
  • Support volunteer mentor recruitment, screening coordination, preparation, and ongoing engagement in collaboration with relevant teams.
  • Escalate significant personnel matters to the Director and work together on appropriate next steps.

Family Engagement, Partnerships, and Coordination

  • Support responsive, culturally respectful communication with youth and families, including program information, registration, attendance, and follow-up.
  • Coordinate program delivery with schools, community organizations, outdoor education partners, vendors, and other collaborators; support the Director in cultivating strategic relationships.
  • Help gather and incorporate youth and family feedback, and identify opportunities for alumni and advisory group engagement.
  • Collaborate with Camping, Enrollment, IT, Research & Evaluation, and other internal teams to address operational needs and improve participant experience.

Data, Compliance, and Resource Stewardship

  • Ensure timely, accurate participant and program records in Salesforce/FreshForce and other approved systems; monitor data quality and staff compliance with established processes.
  • Partner with the Director and Research & Evaluation to track program milestones, attendance, outcomes, and key performance indicators; help implement improvements based on findings.
  • Oversee routine purchasing, supplies, and operational spending within approved budgets and purchasing procedures; provide information to support the Director’s budget management.
  • Implement and reinforce program manuals, safety protocols, background-check procedures, and other organizational requirements in coordination with responsible departments.

Other responsibilities as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree preferred.
  • Minimum 5–7 years of experience in youth programming, education, nonprofit management, or community engagement.
  • Demonstrated success supervising staff and/or volunteers and fostering strong team culture.
  • Experience designing or improving program systems, curricula, or training models.
  • Strong operational and logistical planning skills, particularly across multi-site or field-based programming.
  • Skilled communicator with the ability to facilitate trainings, represent program goals, and engage external partners.
  • Experienced working with diverse youth, families, and community partners.
  • Experience with data-informed program improvement.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office; Salesforce or similar CRM experience preferred.
  • Bilingual (Spanish or Mandarin) and valid driver’s license a plus.
  • Passion for youth development, equity, and The Fresh Air Fund’s mission of providing transformative outdoor experience.
  • Willingness to work evenings/weekends as required by program activities.
  • Ability to spend significant amounts of time outdoors/all seasons.
  • As part of our commitment to maintaining a safe and healthy workplace, The Fresh Air Fund requires all employees to meet applicable vaccination requirements in accordance with federal, state, and local laws. As new public health issues arise, The Fresh Air Fund may require additional vaccinations. Proof of vaccination or an approved exemption will be required as a condition of employment, if applicable.

This “at-will” position is full-time, based in our New York City office, and currently requires three days a week in the office. The Fresh Air Fund offices are open and available all week, and all employees are permitted and encouraged to come to the office to work. Fresh Air may modify its remote work policy generally or with respect to any position at any time.

Salary & Benefits

The salary for this “at-will” position is $70,000-$80,000, commensurate with experience. The Fresh Air Fund offers a generous benefits package including medical, dental and vision insurance, flexible spending accounts, commuter benefits, and employer and employee retirement contribution plans.

Application Instructions: To apply, please submit your resume and cover letter. We are hiring on a rolling basis and encourage interested applicants to apply as early as possible. No calls or recruiters, please.

The Fresh Air Fund is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, committed to inclusive hiring, and dedicated to diversity in its work and on its staff. We strongly encourage candidates of all identities, experiences, orientations and communities to apply.

Benefits

DESCRIPTION:

  • Education: High school diploma or equivalent required. Degree or technical certification a plus.

  • Flexibility: Willingness to work flexible hours, including evenings and weekends, if necessary.

WORK ENVIRONMENT & PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Working Setting: The role is primarily based in a warehouse and food production environment with wet, hot and humid conditions
  • Team Collaboration: Frequent interaction with team members and other departments, requiring effective communication and collaboration.
  • Noise Level: The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate, with some loud noises
