title: Director of Individual Giving
location: Riverside: 3600 Lime Street, Bldg. #2, Riverside, CA, Riverside, CA, US
description:
Title: Director of Individual Giving

Employment Type: Full-time, Exempt
Wage:Annual salary range of $130,000 – $145,000 base pay
Department: Philanthropy
Reports To: Vice President of Philanthropy
Position Location: California – Oakland, Los Angeles, Riverside, Sacramento, Fresno
Work Schedule: Four-Day Work Week: Two (2) days in office, two (2) days remote. However, there may be certain circumstances, like pressing deadlines or peak business periods, where it becomes necessary for the organization to temporarily switch to a five-day work week.


This is one position, posted in five locations. The selected candidate can be based in our Oakland, Sacramento, Riverside, Fresno, or Los Angeles office.

WHY THIS ROLE, WHY NOW

Individual supporters are the foundation of a durable movement. Whether someone gives monthly or makes a significant annual commitment, every gift reflects the same thing: a belief in the work and a desire to be part of it. The strongest individual giving programs honor that belief. They build lasting relationships, keep supporters close to the work, and help every donor see the change they are making possible.

The Director of Individual Giving leads that work across our full donor base. This role oversees major gifts, annual giving, and events strategy. Raising funds across our C3, C4, and PAC entities, the Director shapes a strategy that grows individual revenue, keeps donors for the long term, and connects every supporter to bold climate and justice work. If you are a strategic fundraiser and team leader who wants your work to fuel real political power, we want to hear from you.

WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE DISTINCTIVE

  • Four-day work week for most of the year, with five-day weeks during peak periods.
  • Leadership of a full individual giving program, from small-dollar recurring donations to major gifts, across C3, C4, and PAC fundraising.
  • The chance to build a planned giving program from the start and shape its long-term strategy.
  • A leadership seat on the Philanthropy Team, working closely with the VP of Philanthropy on overall strategy and board fundraising.
  • Work that matters: every donor you bring in fuels voter organizing, electing climate champions, and bold climate policy.
  • Comprehensive benefits package, including health, vision, and dental coverage, 401(k) with employer match, 12 days PTO, 12 holidays, a year-end office closure between Christmas and New Year, and additional benefits that support employee well-being and work-life balance.

POSITION SUMMARY

As a senior leader on the Philanthropy Team, the Director of Individual Giving reports to the Vice President of Philanthropy and is accountable for meeting annual individual giving revenue goals. The Director manages the Deputy Director of Major Gifts, the Development Associate, and part-time Fundraising Callers, building a team culture rooted in donor-centered care, collaboration, and growth. The role works closely with the VP of Philanthropy on fundraising strategy and with the communications team on online and direct mail campaigns. It also leads the design and launch of a revamped planned giving program. The Director sets goals, tracks performance, and uses donor data to guide decisions so the program becomes more effective every year.

KEY PRIORITIES

Lead major giving and PAC fundraising (50%)

  • Manage a personal portfolio of major donors and prospects, raising $1.5M annually through cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
  • Oversee the individual major gifts program, including strategy, moves management, and revenue goals, in partnership with the Deputy Director of Major Gifts.
  • Develop pipeline strategies that identify, qualify, and upgrade donors across all giving levels.
  • Set PAC fundraising strategy with the VP, personally solicit PAC gifts, and coordinate PAC asks to donors across the team's portfolios.

Cultivate and steward donors through events (10%)

  • Coordinate with the Associate Director of Events and Philanthropic Engagement so each event advances prospecting, solicitation, and stewardship goals.
  • Engage donors at events and lead follow-up.

Build a strong annual giving program (15%)

  • Direct the annual giving program, raising $500K annually with a focus on acquisition, retention, and upgrades.
  • Produce three direct mail pieces a year, including managing the calendar, messaging, segmentation, vendor relationships, and results tracking.
  • Oversee the Fundraising Callers program by directing strategy, scripts, lists, and metrics.
  • Partner with the communications team on email and online fundraising campaigns.
  • Draft the general donor update from the department's stewardship talking points.

Lead the team and strengthen operations (25%)

  • Supervise, coach, and mentor the Deputy Director of Major Gifts, including weekly portfolio reviews, and oversee the Annual Giving team.
  • Set metrics, track performance, and report on progress toward revenue goals.
  • Set strategy for the Eco Power Caucus and establish the framework and policies for planned giving, both carried out day to day by the Deputy Director.
  • Partner with the Database Manager to ensure clean data, accurate gift processing, and useful reporting in Raiser’s Edge NXT.
  • Ensure individual giving practices meet compliance requirements for C3, C4, and PAC fundraising.
  • Lead team meetings and internal coordination, and pursue ongoing professional development.

WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU

  • Seven or more years of fundraising experience, including at least five years leading an annual giving program and/or soliciting major gifts
  • A proven record of personally cultivating and closing major gifts
  • Experience with political, PAC, or advocacy fundraising and a working understanding of the differences between C3, C4, and PAC giving
  • Experience managing and developing fundraising staff
  • Working knowledge of multichannel fundraising, including direct mail, digital, phone, and events
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to use data to set goals, segment donors, and measure results
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including compelling solicitations and donor communications
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; experience with Raiser's Edge NXT or a similar CRM
  • Discretion and the ability to maintain confidentiality
  • Passion for environmental protection, racial justice, and meaningful social change

ADDITIONAL STRENGTHS WE WELCOME

  • Experience building or managing a planned giving program
  • Experience with giving societies or leadership-level donor programs
  • Familiarity with Community Centric Fundraising principles
  • Background in nonprofit management, political science, communications, environmental science, or a related field

WHAT ELSE YOU SHOULD KNOW
California Environmental Voters and the California Environmental Voters Education Fund are committed to workplace diversity and inclusion. We are equal opportunity employers and do not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, national origin, ancestry, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, pregnancy (including childbirth, breastfeeding, and related medical conditions), reproductive health decision making, marital status, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

California Environmental Voters and the California Environmental Voters Education Fund have a deep commitment to equity and fostering a culture of inclusion. We invite and encourage applications from all qualified individuals, including those from groups traditionally underrepresented in employment, who may contribute to further diversifying our organization.

If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application process, please contact HR@envirovoters.org.

Founded in 1990 in Queens, New York, the company has grown from a footwear startup into a globally recognized fashion organization with a portfolio of leading brands, including Steve Madden, Kurt Geiger London, Dolce Vita, Betsey Johnson, Carvela, Blondo, and ATM.

With a presence in more than 80 countries, Steve Madden operates across wholesale, retail, e-commerce, licensing, and private label businesses. The company is driven by creativity, individuality, and a fast-paced entrepreneurial spirit, bringing fashion-forward products to consumers around the world.

General Summary:

The Assistant Handbag Designer is responsible for supporting the Design Director and Senior Designers in the development of seasonal handbag collections from concept through production. This role provides critical support throughout the design and product development process, ensuring accuracy, organization, and timely execution across all handbag accounts. The position supports the Wholesale Handbags business.

The responsibilities described below are considered essential functions of the role. This position is based in our NYC office and requires working on-site five days per week.

Major Responsibilities:

Support the Design Director and Senior Designers in the development of seasonal handbag assortments for Wholesale and Off-Price accounts.

Assist the design team throughout all stages of the design process, ensuring alignment with the seasonal calendar across multiple product categories, including handbags, gifting, and small leather goods (SLGs).

Create detailed CAD drawings, technical sketches, and renderings using Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop for client presentations, sample development, and vendor communication.

Create, update, and maintain specification sheets, ensuring design details, construction information, and materials are accurate throughout development and production.

Maintain color standards by tracking lab dips, organizing approval samples, and updating seasonal color charts.

Organize and manage material, color, trim, and hardware libraries, ensuring all design resources are current and accessible.

Prepare presentation boards, sample reviews, and materials for market meetings, client presentations, and internal design reviews.

Maintain and organize the sample closet, accurately tracking incoming and outgoing samples and development pieces.

Collaborate with Technical Design and Product Development teams to ensure design intent and specifications are communicated clearly and executed accurately.

Track sample development progress and proactively follow up with overseas factories and cross-functional teams to meet key milestones and deadlines.

Build and maintain strong working relationships with overseas vendors and factories to support timely sample execution and development needs.

Assist in maintaining seasonal line lists, development trackers, and other design documentation.

Support cross-functional communication with Production, Technical Design, Merchandising, and Sales teams throughout the product lifecycle.

Manage multiple projects simultaneously while maintaining a high level of accuracy, organization, and attention to detail.

Perform other duties and special projects as assigned.

Skills:

Ability to multitask effectively and adapt quickly to changing priorities while maintaining progress on existing projects.

Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

Working knowledge of handbag construction, materials, hardware, and trims.

Experience working with leather, PVC, and other handbag materials preferred.

Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.

Ability to work collaboratively within a team environment while demonstrating initiative and ownership of assigned responsibilities.

Education, Licenses, Certificates, Registrations and/or Experience:

Bachelor's degree in Fashion Design, Accessories Design, or a related field.

1-3 years of design experience, preferably in handbags, accessories, or related categories.

Strong creative eye with an understanding of current market trends and consumer preferences.

Excellent illustration, sketching, and visual presentation skills.

Understanding of handbag construction, materials, hardware, and manufacturing processes.

Proficiency in Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop.

Working knowledge of Microsoft Office, including Excel, Word, and Outlook.

Strong organizational, time-management, and project-management skills.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Ability to prioritize workload and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

Detail-oriented, proactive, and highly motivated.

Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and overseas vendors.

title: IT Operations & Cybersecurity Specialist
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an IT Operations & Cybersecurity Specialist based in Sweden.

Join a distributed technology team dedicated to delivering reliable IT operations and strengthening cybersecurity for organisations that handle sensitive data. In this remote, hands-on role, you will manage day-to-day IT administration, support users, and maintain secure digital environments for multiple clients. You will work with modern cloud productivity platforms, endpoint management tools, and automation technologies to ensure systems remain secure, compliant, and operational. Beyond routine IT support, you will contribute to security initiatives involving vulnerability research, device hardening, and incident response documentation. This position offers an opportunity to develop your cybersecurity expertise while taking ownership of operational responsibilities. You will thrive in an autonomous, asynchronous working environment that values reliability, continuous learning, and practical problem-solving.

Accountabilities

  • IT Administration: Provision and manage user accounts, groups, permissions, and licences across Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, ensuring secure and efficient access to business applications.
  • Endpoint Management: Prepare and onboard Windows and macOS laptops into mobile device management (MDM) platforms, coordinate remote device handovers, and maintain appropriate device configurations.
  • Technical Support: Handle first-line support requests, including password resets, access issues, and routine troubleshooting, while escalating more complex incidents when necessary.
  • IT Maintenance and Monitoring: Conduct weekly maintenance checks covering software patch status, backup logs, security alerts, and general system health to help maintain reliable operations.
  • Documentation and Process Improvement: Document technical fixes, standard operating procedures, and runbooks to improve consistency, knowledge sharing, and operational efficiency.
  • Cybersecurity Projects: Dedicate approximately 20% of your time to security-focused initiatives, including CVE research and briefings, laptop hardening scripts, incident-response playbooks, and ISO 27001 checklist development.
  • Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities to streamline IT workflows, strengthen security practices, and improve service delivery across a distributed client environment.

Requirements

  • Professional Experience: At least two years of hands-on experience in IT operations, helpdesk support, systems administration, or a comparable technical role.
  • Cloud Administration: Practical experience administering Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, including user and group management, security policies, permissions, and basic troubleshooting.
  • Endpoint Management: Familiarity with MDM solutions such as Microsoft Intune, Jamf, or equivalent platforms, including device enrolment and configuration.
  • Scripting and Automation: Proficiency in at least one scripting language, such as PowerShell, Bash, or Python, with the ability to automate routine tasks and improve operational workflows.
  • Communication Skills: Strong written and spoken English, with the ability to document technical processes clearly and collaborate effectively with distributed teams. German language skills are an advantage.
  • Remote Working Readiness: A reliable internet connection, a professional remote working environment, and the ability to work independently across different time zones.
  • Personal Attributes: A proactive, organised, and detail-oriented approach, with strong troubleshooting skills, sound judgement, and a willingness to learn and take ownership of responsibilities.
  • Preferred Qualifications: Microsoft 365 Administrator Expert, Microsoft 365 Endpoint Administrator, or Google Workspace Administrator certifications are advantageous.
  • Security Knowledge: Exposure to cybersecurity and compliance frameworks such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, or similar standards is a plus.

Benefits

  • Competitive Compensation: Hourly compensation within the advertised range of €10–€18, with the original role description specifying a typical rate of €12–€16 per hour, paid in euros.
  • Fully Remote Work: Work remotely from anywhere.
  • Autonomy and Ownership: Take responsibility for your area of work, manage your tasks independently, and contribute directly to operational improvements.
  • Professional Development: Build practical cybersecurity experience through hands-on projects involving vulnerability research, endpoint hardening, incident response, and compliance.
  • Career Growth: Opportunity to expand your responsibilities and progress into a broader role as the team grows.
  • Flexible, Asynchronous Culture: Benefit from an async-first working environment, with occasional video meetings scheduled during hours compatible with Central European Time (CET).
  • Practical Security Experience: Develop your technical capabilities while working across IT administration, endpoint management, automation, and security operations.

title: On-Call Youth Site Specialist - Home Youth Services
description:
OUR MISSION: MWVCAA invests in people and their futures to reduce the impacts of poverty.

Our Vision: We envision a just future, where our communities are empowered to reach positive outcomes and everyone is respected for their infinite worth.

Working at MWVCAA means becoming part of a mission-driven community dedicated to equity, dignity, and opportunity for all. We offer competitive pay, a rich company culture that values diversity, and an array of benefits - but we consider the best benefit here to be the reward of helping those in our community live better lives. Come find meaningful work and bring your skills as a On-Call Youth Site Specialist. The Youth Site Specialist (YSS) directly supervises at-risk youth and assists youth in obtaining basic needs and navigating resources, while ensuring a safe space at the HOME Youth Services shelters. In addition to assisting with basic shelter services, they are the point person for building connections, mentoring, and providing valuable resources to youth residents. This team offers a lot of growth opportunities and professional development through hands-on experience.

This position will be serving both Marion and Polk counties and is On Call up to 19 hours weekly.

title: Kubernetes Engineer
description:
Description

Quantum Sky is searching for a Kubernetes Engineer to support the US Space Force’s Space Systems Command (SSC), Operational Command and Control Acquisition Delta, known as Kobayashi Maru. Kobayashi Maru is responsible for continuously delivering impactful software for space operations. The program office’s mission includes the development and deployment of software for space defense, space domain awareness, and enabling data services.

Responsibilities:

  • Leveraging Kubernetes technology to deliver, install, upgrade, patch and maintain highly reliable and resilient solutions for deploying and hosting current and future tools and services needed to develop, test, secure, and ship software applications to production.
  • Perform within an Agile framework including conducting daily stand up, welcome feedback often, sprint/iteration planning, duration planning, retrospectives, executing from the product backlog and roadmap, meeting performance metrics, and reporting on progress and blockers.
  • Securing and configuring containerized services orchestrated with Kubernetes, and its underlying environment.
  • Tuning Kubernetes performance and identifying problems by using service and traffic metrics by establishing monitoring and alerting dashboards.
  • Lead for the lifecycle management of all containerized services used in the development of Kobayashi Maru software.

title: Principal Technical Program Manager, Network Delivery Engineering
location: Atlanta, GA, USA; Thornton, CO, USA
description:
A problem isn’t truly solved until it’s solved for all. That’s why Googlers build products that help create opportunities for everyone, whether down the street or across the globe. As a Technical Program Manager at Google, you’ll use your technical expertise to lead complex, multi-disciplinary projects from start to finish. You’ll work with stakeholders to plan requirements, identify risks, manage project schedules, and communicate clearly with cross-functional partners across the company. You're equally comfortable explaining your team's analyses and recommendations to executives as you are discussing the technical tradeoffs in product development with engineers.

Google's Global Network Infrastructure powers the world's largest compute, storage, and AI/ML workloads, spanning hyperscale data centers, optical networks, subsea cables, and the edge. Network Delivery Engineering is the critical operational bridge between upstream network technology development and downstream global deployment.

As Google's AI/ML and Cloud infrastructure scales, we are fundamentally re-engineering how we deliver networks, transforming our delivery engine from bespoke execution to a high-throughput, predictable production system. Our mission is to re-engineer delivery for throughput.

As a Principal Technical Program Manager, you will be the lead architect re-engineering our end-to-end network delivery lifecycle. At the intersection of network engineering, process engineering, and systems thinking, you will treat the entire delivery pipeline, from architectural intent and New Product Introduction (NPI) to material orchestration, automated provisioning, and field turnup, as a single integrated system. You will diagnose bottlenecks, redesign cross-functional workflows, define automation requirements, and standardize engineering standards to unlock step-function gains in delivery velocity, quality, and scale.

Behind everything our users see online is the architecture built by the Technical Infrastructure team to keep it running. From developing and maintaining our data centers to building the next generation of Google platforms, we make Google's product portfolio possible. We're proud to be our engineers' engineers and love voiding warranties by taking things apart so we can rebuild them. We keep our networks up and running, ensuring our users have the best and fastest experience possible.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $240000 - $333000 (USD) + 25% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google.
  • Apply systems thinking to map and re-engineer the end-to-end network delivery value stream across data centers, AI/ML fabrics, and WAN, unifying hardware design, planning, supply chain, software, and field execution.
  • Lead high-impact transformations using process engineering methodologies (e.g., Lean/Six Sigma) to compress Concept-to-GA cycle times, eliminating manual handoffs and systemic rework.
  • Re-architect onboarding for next-generation hardware, optical interconnects, and SDN software, embedding zero-touch automation and testability upstream into design phases (EVT/DVT/PVT).
  • Partner with engineering teams to translate processes into automated workflows and AI-enabled guardrails, while defining metrics and feedback loops to predict delivery risks and drive root-cause elimination.
  • Serve as an Executive Staff Advisor, resolving high-ambiguity technical deadlocks across Platform Engineering, Supply Chain, and Global Operations at the VP/Director level.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in a technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 10 years of experience in program management.
  • Experience in technical program management or process engineering for physical products, hardware systems, network/data center infrastructure, or manufacturing/supply chain operations.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Master's degree or PhD in Engineering, Operations Research, or a related technical field.
  • 15 years of experience architecting hyperscale network deployment, hardware/software integration, or supply chain delivery systems.
  • Experience at a Principal (Senior Staff) level, synthesizing ambiguous, cross-organizational challenges into actionable roadmaps and influencing VP/Director-level stakeholders.
  • Deep expertise in systems thinking, with a proven ability to redesign complex, interdependent workflows to eliminate systemic bottlenecks and failure modes.
  • Track record of achieving step-function improvements (e.g., cycle-time reduction) in hyperscale data center or global telecom environments.

title: Product Manager Privacy
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Product Manager Privacy based in Germany.

Take ownership of privacy and consent management across a suite of digital advertising products spanning web, mobile apps, and connected TV (CTV). In this strategic product role, you will lead the Privacy squad and report directly to the VP of Product, shaping how consent signals are collected, interpreted, and transmitted across multiple advertising channels. Your mission is to maximize publisher revenue while ensuring compliance with applicable privacy regulations and industry standards. You will translate complex legal frameworks into practical product specifications, balancing regulatory obligations with commercial opportunities. Working closely with engineering, analytics, UX, engagement teams, and privacy experts, you will drive measurable improvements in consent management and monetization. Join a fast-growing, international, AI-driven environment where analytical thinking, ownership, and pragmatic decision-making are central to success.

Accountabilities:

As Product Manager Privacy, you will own the consent management strategy, lead the Privacy squad, and ensure that privacy requirements are consistently implemented across products and channels. Your main responsibilities will include:

  • Consent Engine and Frameworks: Own the FastCMP consent signal engine roadmap, covering IAB TCF, GPP, Global Privacy Control (GPC), Google Consent Mode, and US privacy signals. Define the applicable frameworks and default behaviors for each jurisdiction, and deliver new standard versions on time across web, mobile, and CTV.

  • Cross-Product Privacy Rules: Translate legislation and industry standards into clear product specifications for Actirise, Viously, and Meetscale across web, app, and CTV. Maintain a compliance checklist for consent-related initiatives and coordinate with product managers to ensure signals are correctly collected, respected, and transmitted.

  • Privacy-Compliant Monetization: Identify opportunities to monetize traffic within applicable privacy rules. Distinguish mandatory requirements from recommendations, assess revenue implications before making decisions, and evaluate options for traffic with no or partial consent, including legitimate interest, contextual advertising, and no-ad requirements.

  • Measurement and Decision-Making: Apply a measure-before-deciding approach, ensuring traffic is not rejected or degraded without supporting measurements and a documented decision.

  • Compliance, Vendors, and Certifications: Own IAB TCF and Google CMP certifications, manage vendor lists and custom vendors, and mitigate the risk of deregistration. Work with the Data Protection Officer (DPO) to validate privacy interpretations while retaining product ownership of decisions.

  • Client and Partner Engagement: Serve as the product point of contact for strategic clients and partners on privacy matters, including CMP migrations, regulatory requests, and buyer requirements.

  • Regulatory and Standards Monitoring: Track upcoming legislation and industry standards, anticipate their product implications, and translate them into roadmap priorities before they become urgent.

  • AI-Ready Product Management: Apply an agentic-first approach by ensuring privacy rules and configurations can be executed by AI agents, supported by clean data contracts and appropriate access controls.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Engagement, UX Orchestration, Analytics, FastCMP engineering, and the DPO to coordinate consent templates, A/B testing, CMP and paywall configurations, and privacy signal measurement.

    • Requirements:

    The ideal candidate combines substantial privacy expertise with hands-on product management experience in advertising technology. You understand how to interpret legal requirements without unnecessarily restricting legitimate business opportunities, and you can translate complex rules into actionable technical specifications. The following qualifications are expected:

    • Privacy and Product Experience: At least 5 years of experience in privacy, consent management platforms (CMPs), or ad tech, including product management experience and a proven track record of shipping products in this ecosystem.

    • Industry Standards and Regulations: Strong knowledge of IAB TCF, Global Privacy Platform (GPP), OpenRTB consent fields, GDPR, ePrivacy, and US privacy legislation, including CCPA and applicable state laws.

    • Commercial and Analytical Judgment: Ability to distinguish legal obligations from recommendations and support product decisions with data, evidence, and measurable revenue impact.

    • Technical Specification Skills: Ability to write precise, implementation-ready specifications that engineers can execute with minimal clarification. Programming experience is not required.

    • Data-Driven Approach: Familiarity with basic SQL, dashboards, analytics, and A/B testing, with a commitment to measuring outcomes before making decisions.

    • AI and Agentic Workflows: Daily use of an AI assistant, such as Claude, and practical experience building AI-enabled skills or agentic workflows within product management.

    • Communication Skills: Fluent in both English and French, with the ability to communicate effectively with legal specialists, engineers, product teams, clients, and business stakeholders.

    • Problem-Solving Mindset: Pragmatic, analytical, and comfortable making decisions in a fast-moving environment. You understand the Pareto principle and know how to prioritize high-impact improvements.

title: Dansk Kundeservicemedarbejder – Remote i Holland
description:
Reference: TENE

Om Holland:

Kanaler, diger, træsko og tulipaner. Ting, man ofte finder på postkort fra Holland, men som langt fra fortæller hele historien om det smukke, cykelglade land. Holland tilbyder mange jobmuligheder i et internationalt arbejdsmiljø, hvor særligt kyndige medarbejdere inden for medicin, teknologi, IT og marketing er hjerteligt velkomne. Kunden er GROHE, og de søger i øjeblikket danske kundeservicemedarbejdere til at yde support til kunder med GROHE-produkter.

I din rolle som GROHEs kundeservicemedarbejder kommer du til at beskæftige dig med forskellige opgaver, når kunderne oplever forskellige udfordringer. Hvis du bor mere end en time væk fra byen, sørger vi for et hotel i den uge. Efter uddannelsen kan du arbejde hjemmefra, men hvis du foretrækker at arbejde på kontoret i Zoetermeer, er du også velkommen til det!

💪🏻 Fremragende problemløsningsevner med ekstraordinære evner til at opbygge interpersonelle relationer.

🥇 Evne til at håndtere flere, konkurrerende prioriteter, pligter og opgaver, og du har fremragende kommunikationsevner og kan udtrykke dine tanker klart og koncist.

Hvis du har spørgsmål til stillingen, er du velkommen til at sende en e-mail til . Der sidder en medarbejder klar til at hjælpe med at besvare spørgsmål.

title: Director of Individual Giving
location: Fresno: 2721 Ventura Blvd., #104, Fresno, CA, Fresno, CA, US
description:
Title: Director of Individual Giving

Employment Type: Full-time, Exempt
Wage:Annual salary range of $130,000 – $145,000 base pay
Department: Philanthropy
Reports To: Vice President of Philanthropy
Position Location: California – Oakland, Los Angeles, Riverside, Sacramento, Fresno
Work Schedule: Four-Day Work Week: Two (2) days in office, two (2) days remote. However, there may be certain circumstances, like pressing deadlines or peak business periods, where it becomes necessary for the organization to temporarily switch to a five-day work week.


This is one position, posted in five locations. The selected candidate can be based in our Oakland, Sacramento, Riverside, Fresno, or Los Angeles office.

WHY THIS ROLE, WHY NOW

Individual supporters are the foundation of a durable movement. Whether someone gives monthly or makes a significant annual commitment, every gift reflects the same thing: a belief in the work and a desire to be part of it. The strongest individual giving programs honor that belief. They build lasting relationships, keep supporters close to the work, and help every donor see the change they are making possible.

The Director of Individual Giving leads that work across our full donor base. This role oversees major gifts, annual giving, and events strategy. Raising funds across our C3, C4, and PAC entities, the Director shapes a strategy that grows individual revenue, keeps donors for the long term, and connects every supporter to bold climate and justice work. If you are a strategic fundraiser and team leader who wants your work to fuel real political power, we want to hear from you.

WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE DISTINCTIVE

  • Four-day work week for most of the year, with five-day weeks during peak periods.
  • Leadership of a full individual giving program, from small-dollar recurring donations to major gifts, across C3, C4, and PAC fundraising.
  • The chance to build a planned giving program from the start and shape its long-term strategy.
  • A leadership seat on the Philanthropy Team, working closely with the VP of Philanthropy on overall strategy and board fundraising.
  • Work that matters: every donor you bring in fuels voter organizing, electing climate champions, and bold climate policy.
  • Comprehensive benefits package, including health, vision, and dental coverage, 401(k) with employer match, 12 days PTO, 12 holidays, a year-end office closure between Christmas and New Year, and additional benefits that support employee well-being and work-life balance.

POSITION SUMMARY

As a senior leader on the Philanthropy Team, the Director of Individual Giving reports to the Vice President of Philanthropy and is accountable for meeting annual individual giving revenue goals. The Director manages the Deputy Director of Major Gifts, the Development Associate, and part-time Fundraising Callers, building a team culture rooted in donor-centered care, collaboration, and growth. The role works closely with the VP of Philanthropy on fundraising strategy and with the communications team on online and direct mail campaigns. It also leads the design and launch of a revamped planned giving program. The Director sets goals, tracks performance, and uses donor data to guide decisions so the program becomes more effective every year.

KEY PRIORITIES

Lead major giving and PAC fundraising (50%)

  • Manage a personal portfolio of major donors and prospects, raising $1.5M annually through cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
  • Oversee the individual major gifts program, including strategy, moves management, and revenue goals, in partnership with the Deputy Director of Major Gifts.
  • Develop pipeline strategies that identify, qualify, and upgrade donors across all giving levels.
  • Set PAC fundraising strategy with the VP, personally solicit PAC gifts, and coordinate PAC asks to donors across the team's portfolios.

Cultivate and steward donors through events (10%)

  • Coordinate with the Associate Director of Events and Philanthropic Engagement so each event advances prospecting, solicitation, and stewardship goals.
  • Engage donors at events and lead follow-up.

Build a strong annual giving program (15%)

  • Direct the annual giving program, raising $500K annually with a focus on acquisition, retention, and upgrades.
  • Produce three direct mail pieces a year, including managing the calendar, messaging, segmentation, vendor relationships, and results tracking.
  • Oversee the Fundraising Callers program by directing strategy, scripts, lists, and metrics.
  • Partner with the communications team on email and online fundraising campaigns.
  • Draft the general donor update from the department's stewardship talking points.

Lead the team and strengthen operations (25%)

  • Supervise, coach, and mentor the Deputy Director of Major Gifts, including weekly portfolio reviews, and oversee the Annual Giving team.
  • Set metrics, track performance, and report on progress toward revenue goals.
  • Set strategy for the Eco Power Caucus and establish the framework and policies for planned giving, both carried out day to day by the Deputy Director.
  • Partner with the Database Manager to ensure clean data, accurate gift processing, and useful reporting in Raiser’s Edge NXT.
  • Ensure individual giving practices meet compliance requirements for C3, C4, and PAC fundraising.
  • Lead team meetings and internal coordination, and pursue ongoing professional development.

WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU

  • Seven or more years of fundraising experience, including at least five years leading an annual giving program and/or soliciting major gifts
  • A proven record of personally cultivating and closing major gifts
  • Experience with political, PAC, or advocacy fundraising and a working understanding of the differences between C3, C4, and PAC giving
  • Experience managing and developing fundraising staff
  • Working knowledge of multichannel fundraising, including direct mail, digital, phone, and events
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to use data to set goals, segment donors, and measure results
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including compelling solicitations and donor communications
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; experience with Raiser's Edge NXT or a similar CRM
  • Discretion and the ability to maintain confidentiality
  • Passion for environmental protection, racial justice, and meaningful social change

ADDITIONAL STRENGTHS WE WELCOME

  • Experience building or managing a planned giving program
  • Experience with giving societies or leadership-level donor programs
  • Familiarity with Community Centric Fundraising principles
  • Background in nonprofit management, political science, communications, environmental science, or a related field

WHAT ELSE YOU SHOULD KNOW
California Environmental Voters and the California Environmental Voters Education Fund are committed to workplace diversity and inclusion. We are equal opportunity employers and do not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, national origin, ancestry, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, pregnancy (including childbirth, breastfeeding, and related medical conditions), reproductive health decision making, marital status, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

California Environmental Voters and the California Environmental Voters Education Fund have a deep commitment to equity and fostering a culture of inclusion. We invite and encourage applications from all qualified individuals, including those from groups traditionally underrepresented in employment, who may contribute to further diversifying our organization.

If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application process, please contact HR@envirovoters.org.

title: Senior Operational Risk and Reporting Analyst
description:
Mission
Groq is seeking a Senior Operational Risk and Reporting Analyst to build GRC risk reporting into a continuous operation that tells leadership a story in business impact terms rather than by control, and to own the third party risk program. You will turn a once-a-year risk exercise into a monthly operating rhythm, and track remediation across every framework in the program.

Responsibilities & opportunities in this role:
  • Build and run GRC risk reporting as a continuous operation: intake, scoring against the risk methodology, treatment tracking, and risk acceptance with owners and expiry dates; centralise risk data (register, KRIs, audit findings, critical vendors) into dashboards leadership can use.
  • Produce the monthly risk report to security leadership, framed by business impact rather than control count, with executive-ready commentary.
  • Own the third party risk program end to end: vendor tiering, security assessments on the cadence each tier requires, review of vendor SOC 2 and ISO reports, remediation tracking, and clearing the vendor assessment control in GRC tool.
  • Track remediation across all frameworks so every open finding has an owner, a date and a disposition, and report aging monthly.

Ideal candidates have/are:
  • 5+ years in operational risk, IT risk or GRC, including building and running risk assessment and reporting processes end to end in a regulated environment.
  • Experience producing monthly risk reporting for risk committees and executives.
  • Experience testing controls for effectiveness, evaluating new initiatives for risk exposure before implementation, including third party risk assessments.
  • Experience with GRC tooling preferred.

Why Join Us:
  • Purposeful Hiring: You’re not here by accident, and neither is anyone else. Every teammate is handpicked with intention because who we build with matters.
  • Builders Wanted: You’re not just riding the rocket ship, you’re building it. Your work directly shapes the trajectory of our company.
  • Mission-Driven Work: We’re here to make a real impact. Our mission fuels everything we do.
  • Tackling Hard Problems: If easy isn’t your thing, you’re in the right place. We solve some of the most complex and exciting challenges in our space.
  • Excellence Is The Standard: High performance isn’t just encouraged, it’s the baseline. And it’s contagious.

Compensation
Groq is committed to providing competitive compensation through our Total Cash philosophy, which incorporates potential bonus value directly into base pay. The total cash salary range for this position, which is inclusive of the potential bonus value, is $127,500–$172,500, with individual placement determined by your geographic location, experience, skills, and alignment with internal compensation standards. This range is specific to candidates located in the United States. Compensation for international candidates will vary based on local market dynamics. Beyond cash compensation, Groq also offers a Long-Term Incentive (LTI) Program and a robust suite of employee benefits.

description:

We are driven by a mission to connect the world for good and our people make it possible. Every single day, the creativity, dedication and genuine care for our communities are what push us forward and make this a truly special place to be.

Who You Are:

As the you Vice President, Regional External Affairs you are responsible for developing and executing QTS's external affairs strategy across an assigned multi-state region. You oversee government relations, public policy, legislative advocacy, economic development, permitting and zoning, community engagement, stakeholder relations, and public affairs activities that support QTS's growth, development, operations, and long-term reputation. Reporting directly to the Chief External Affairs Officer, the Vice President serves as a key member of the External Affairs leadership team and leads a regional organization of approximately 10-12 team members. You will partner closely with leaders across Communications, Marketing, Legal, Development, Energy Strategy, Operations, and the Executive Team to advance business priorities, support market expansion, and drive strategic advocacy initiatives. You will build and maintain trusted relationships with elected officials, policymakers, economic development partners, community leaders, industry stakeholders, and internal business partners. Success in the role requires a campaign-oriented mindset, combining strategic planning, disciplined execution, stakeholder engagement, and coalition-building to advance QTS's business objectives and strengthen its position as a trusted community and industry partner.

What You Will Do: (Job Responsibilities)

  • Develop and execute a comprehensive regional external affairs strategy aligned with QTS's growth, development, operational, and public policy objectives.
  • Lead and coordinate integrated advocacy campaigns at the state and local levels to advance business priorities and support market expansion efforts.
  • Direct and develop a high-performing regional team, establishing clear priorities, accountability, performance expectations, and professional development opportunities.
  • Partner closely with cross-functional leaders to align external affairs strategies with corporate objectives and operational priorities.
  • Manage regional operating plans, budgets, consultants, and external resources to support legislative, regulatory, business development, community engagement, and growth priorities.

  • Represent QTS externally as a senior leader and trusted advocate in support of the company's mission, values, and growth objectives.

Government Affairs & Public Policy

Lead government affairs, legislative advocacy, regulatory engagement, and public policy efforts across the region. Develop strategies that advance QTS growth objectives and strengthen relationships with policymakers, regulatory agencies, economic development organizations, and industry stakeholders.


Community Engagement & Reputation

Lead stakeholder engagement strategies that build trust, support development objectives, and enhance QTS's reputation. Serve as QTS's senior regional representative with community leaders, business organizations, educational institutions, and other key stakeholders.


Economic Development & Market Expansion

Partner with Development, Site Selection, Energy Strategy, and Operations teams to support market expansion, site development, infrastructure investments, and growth initiatives. Identify opportunities and mitigate risks that could impact business objectives.


Executive Counsel & Strategic Leadership

Provide strategic advice to senior leadership on political, regulatory, economic, and community dynamics affecting the business. Support high-profile development, policy, permitting, and reputational matters through proactive planning and stakeholder strategy.


Organizational Leadership

Lead and develop a high-performing regional external affairs organization. Drive accountability, operational excellence, resource stewardship, and measurable business outcomes across the region.


Other duties as assigned.

  • Bachelor's degree in public policy, Political Science, Business, Communications, Law, Economics, Urban Planning, or related fields.
  • 12+ years of leadership experience in government affairs, public policy, legislative affairs, lobbying, economic development, public affairs, or external affairs, including responsibility for a multi-state region.

  • Experience leading teams, managing budgets, and driving results across executive-level, cross-functional organizations.
  • Strong understanding of legislative, regulatory, permitting, economic development, and community engagement processes.
  • Experience supporting large-scale infrastructure, energy, technology, real estate, utility, telecommunications, or industrial development projects.

title: Intake Clinician (Peekskill)
description:
Overview

Westchester Jewish Community Services (WJCS) is an award-winning nonprofit, nonsectarian human services organization founded in 1943. Today, it has grown to be the largest provider of licensed outpatient community behavioral health services and one of the largest human service agencies in Westchester County. WJCS delivers innovative programs and services and compassionate care to more than 20,000 people of all ages and backgrounds throughout the county.


We are currently seeking a full-time Intake Clinician to join our team in Peekskill. In this role, you will be responsible for serving as the first clinical point of contact for individuals entering services. This role focuses exclusively on completing intake and assessment processes in a warm, trauma-informed, and efficient manner. The Intake Clinician ensures clients are welcomed, engaged, and connected to care as quickly as possible. This is a fully in-person role - Monday–Friday, 9 AM – 5 PM.

The salary for this full-time position is $80,000 - $85,000, based on licensure, and bilingual (English/Spanish) fluency. In addition, there are opportunties to earn supplemental income.


Responsibilities

As a valued member of our team, your responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

  • Conduct comprehensive biopsychosocial initial assessments.
  • Provide scheduled and rapid access same-day intake evaluations.
  • Assess safety risks and respond appropriately.
  • Develop initial service recommendations and care plans.
  • Facilitate warm handoffs to ongoing providers.
  • Maintain accurate, timely documentation in the electronic medical record.
  • Collaborate with interdisciplinary care teams.
  • Complete 5 to 7 services daily comprised of initial and continuing evaluation appointments.


Requirements

We are seeking candidates who possess the following qualifications:

  • Master’s Degree in Social Work or Mental Health Counseling.
  • NYS licensure (LCSW, LMHC-D) required.
  • Experience conducting behavioral health assessments.
  • Strong engagement, and written and verbal communication skills.
  • Proficiency with computer skills and electronic health records.
  • Ability to work effectively with diverse, multicultural populations.
  • Bilingual English/Spanish fluency preferred.

title: Employee Housing Resident Advisor - Winter 26-27
description:
Job Summary

The Resident Advisor (RA) facilitates the social, work and personal adjustment of international and domestic residents in our Employee Housing facility, Base Camp Lodge. The RA develops a sense of community among residents and serves as a positive role model to residents and peer staff members. The RA enforces the rules and policies of Bear Valley’s Housing agreement with the residents, while maintaining a clean and livable shared areas for all tenants to enjoy. The RA acts as a liaison between residents and Bear Valley administration team.

Job Duties and Responsibilities

This job description is intended as a summary of the primary responsibilities of and the qualifications for the position. The job description is not intended to be inclusive of all duties an individual in the position might be asked to perform or of all the qualifications that may be required now or in the future. We will not ask you to perform a task that is inherently unsafe or that you are not adequately trained to perform. When we do ask for your assistance with any job, we expect an enthusiastic and cooperative response.

  • Provide a warm welcome to new residents, showing them to their rooms, go over policies, etc.
  • Assist with move in/move out procedures, including key distribution and room inspections.
  • Schedule and lead weekly resident meeting – collaborate with HR team on important information to be shared, provide summary of meeting.
  • Be available to perform RA responsibilities, a minimum of 4 hours a day, 5 days a week. Other hours include “on-call” duties to complete a 32-hour work week.
  • One workday each week will be designated for cleaning the Employee Services Office located at the Resort. This day will also be reserved for the weekly collaborative meeting with HR.
  • Be available to respond to all requests and emergencies during “on-call” shifts.
  • Collaborate with HR on behalf of the residents regarding issues of concern to the residents.
  • Provide housing information via electronic or in-house bulletin board.
  • Collaborate with HR Coordinator to design and implement experiences for residents that enhance the social, educational, community, and personal development of residents in Bear Valley.
  • Participate in disciplinary conferences and actions as required with administrative team.
  • Respond to all witnessed violations occurring within basecamp lodge. Prepare and submit the appropriate report to bear valley administrative team within 24 hours.
  • Work with HR Coordinator to create “cleaning teams” and split them up between tenants then proceed to make a weekly schedule advising them of their days and times, ensure cleaning tasks are being completed.
  • Perform daily cleaning tasks as needed, sweeping, mopping, vacuuming, taking out trash, cleaning dishes, toilets, and showers.
  • Stock supplies including toilet paper, paper towels, garbage bags and cleaning supplies. Notify HR when stock gets low.
  • Refill soap and paper towels.
  • Make sure garbage gets into the bins every Sunday.
  • Assist residents in adjustment to roommates and community living.
  • Perform monthly inspections of tenants’ rooms and common areas, ensuring all policies are being followed.
  • Shovel snow at main entrances to ensure tenants can safely enter the building.
  • Communicate with HR Coordinator regularly.
  • Must be organized, self-motivated, and present a professional appearance.
  • Light maintenance duties may be required. Report any damage or breaks to HR/Maintenance.
  • Must be 18 or older to apply.
  • Must be able to pass background check.
  • Other tasks and projects as assigned.

Supervisory responsibilities

Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws. Responsibilities include addressing complaints and resolving problems within the employee housing property. Must be reliable with response times and communication (call, text, and email). You must be comfortable contacting local Sheriff Office in case of emergencies. As RA you serve as a role model for other tenants and are responsible for setting a positive example by following all policies and demonstrating professional conduct.

Cleaning & Maintenance Support

Monitor cleanliness and safety of common areas including lounges, kitchen, hallways, bathrooms and showers. Perform cleaning duties (e.g., wiping surfaces, emptying trash, spot-checking bathrooms). Report maintenance issues or facility damage to appropriate staff promptly. Encourage and model shared responsibility for cleanliness among residents.

Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education and/or experience

High school diploma or general education degree (GED); or one to three months related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Language skills

Ability to read, analyze, and interpret general business periodicals, professional journals, technical procedures, or governmental regulations. Ability to write reports, business correspondence, and procedure manuals. Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from groups of managers, clients, customers, and the general public. Must be able to read and interpret tenant/landlord laws.

Reasoning ability

Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists. Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.

Physical demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to stand, walk, and sit. The employee is occasionally required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; and taste or smell. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 10 pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move more than 50 pounds. This includes moving furniture, setting up of housing operation, coordinating snow removal, light maintenance duties and repairs, and keeping the employee housing common areas neat, clean, and organized.

Rent

RA’s rent will be discounted 100% as payment in lieu of services offered. As RA you are responsible for following and enforcing our policies. If you are unable to perform these tasks immediate disciplinary action will be taken including termination of employment and eviction.

Work Schedules

Weather, snow conditions and the number of guests play a large role in the work scheduling of Bear Valley employees.

When conditions are normal, you may be expected to work 40 up to 48 hours per week, including weekends and holidays. During busy periods – especially the holiday periods in December and the months of January and February – you may be expected to work six (6) days a week.

You must arrange for transportation to work so that you arrive at your designated workstation at the scheduled time. Keep in mind that you will often be required to drive on hilly, snowpacked, and icy roads.

Working Conditions

At any time during the ski season, Bear Valley employees are often required to perform their tasks in high winds, heavy snowfalls, low visibility, rain, and extremely cold or warm temperatures.


Uniforms

A professional appearance at Bear Valley is required. Please always wear your name tag and uniform during your scheduled shift. We will provide most of the uniforms for you to do your job. This uniform is for work hours ONLY, no exceptions.

You will be required to provide some items as part of your job.

The quality, color, and style of the items must be approved by your manager prior to being worn to work. All hats worn must have the Bear Valley logo while on shift.



The skiing/riding employee represents a model for safe skiing for both the guest and fellow employees. You are required to be aware of all safe skiing procedures, trail closures, and out-of-bounds policies of the mountain.

title: Research Manager
description:
About Us:

Good Business Lab (GBL) is a research-to-action nonprofit. We conduct rigorous economics research to advance access to high-quality jobs for low-income workers. We believe a truly good job is more than wages — it creates conditions for workers to thrive. Yet too few workers have access to sustained wage growth, supportive workplaces, and real opportunities for advancement. GBL works to change this by expanding pathways into better-fit, higher-opportunity work and improving job quality within large employers. We study worker needs, partner with workers and employers to co-design interventions that serve both individual and business goals, and evaluate impact through causal methods. Across manufacturing, retail, and food service, our work shows that improving job quality also improves firm performance. Globally, we have directly improved outcomes for over 500,000 workers, with indirect reach across an ecosystem impacting nearly 2 million more.

The founders of the Lab are Achyuta Adhvaryu - Professor of Economics and Director of 21st Century India Center at the School of Global Policy and Strategy, UC San Diego (), Anant Ahuja - Head of ESG and Sustainability at Shahi Exports Pvt. Ltd., and Anant Nyshadham - Assistant Professor of Business Economics and Public Policy at the University of Michigan ().

About the role

Research Managers (RMs) are integral to the success of our randomized evaluations. Working closely with the research team at GBL and collaborating economists and researchers across U.S. universities, the RM will support all key activities to grow our U.S. project portfolio. The RM will support all stages of the research process across two U.S.-based projects, along with other key activities to develop more projects in the U.S. Here is a quick description of the two active projects in the U.S.:

  • AI-assisted job search and matching: Research on using algorithmic matching to connect low-income jobseekers to local vacancies — widening the scope of job search across sectors and improving matching to jobs in which candidates may have no prior experience. This research builds on our prior work on AI-directed job search, which you can read about here.
  • Cash incentives and continuity of care: Research investigating the effects of small cash incentives on continuity of care among the unsheltered population in the Los Angeles region.

To acclimatize yourself with our work, you can explore our website and LinkedIn.

Compensation: $80,000–$100,000 annually, subject to the candidate’s experience, skills, and fit for the role.
Type of Employment: Fixed Term Employment

Duration: 1 year

Location: This is a remote position. Team members are based in Philadelphia, PA (with an office space) and Ann Arbor, MI, and relocation to either location is an option for candidates who are interested.
- Please note, the candidate must be legally authorized to work in the United States.

Roles and Responsibilities:

  • Lead grant writing and prepare reports for funding agencies
  • Mentor Research Assistants and other research staff; assist with hiring and training Research Assistants and other research staff
  • Assist with Research Assistant responsibilities as needed (literature reviews, survey instrument design, data cleaning, survey planning, data quality monitoring, fieldwork supervision, etc.)
  • Ensure projects follow GBL standards and protocols, including IRB approval, coding standards, and analysis procedures
  • Anticipate and identify risks or threats to research design/projects, propose solutions, and escalate to researchers as needed
  • Maintain clear communication and alignment between researchers, GBL staff, and implementation partners; clarify expectations and troubleshoot challenges
  • Ensure the project has sufficient material and human resources
  • Maintain comprehensive project documentation — codebooks, field protocols, and project logs — to academic standards of transparency and reproducibility
  • Coordinate with administrative and finance teams on participant payments and study-related costs
  • Prepare policy memos, research briefs, and communications content (blogs, articles) on ongoing and completed studies
  • Represent GBL at meetings with external stakeholders (e.g., delivering presentations)

Who are you?

  • Master's or doctoral degree in Economics, Statistics, Public Policy, Development Studies, or a related field (or Bachelors degree with 4+ years of relevant work experience)
  • Ability to work in a team, manage multiple projects on the ground and be self-motivated
  • Experience managing Randomized Controlled Trials
  • Extensive experience conducting social science or economic field research (supervising data collection, survey design and implementation, data management, etc.)
  • Strong quantitative and analytical skills, including proficiency in statistical software such as Stata or R, and experience with financial reporting and management
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Word and Excel/spreadsheet applications
  • Strong familiarity with data science principles and AI coding platforms (e.g., Claude Code, Codex/GPT), among others.
  • Detail-oriented with strong written and oral communication skills
  • Willingness to travel occasionally to project sites
  • Experience in grant writing for existing and new projects

Additional Requirements:

What should you be comfortable with?

  • A dynamic environment with competing priorities
  • Working in a team with shared responsibilities
  • Independently coordinating with coworkers to accomplish goals
  • Being resourceful in new environments and scenarios
  • Problem-solving in high-pressure environments
  • Adapting your approach, being focused on the problem and not being stuck to one idea or way of solving a problem

How to apply?

Share the following documents with your application form:

  • Curriculum vitae (CV)
  • A cover letter describing your background, interest in economics research, familiarity with relevant statistical software, and any experience as a research assistant and/or manager or on independent projects.
  • Please include the names and email addresses of two references in your cover letter.

Deadline to Apply:

On rolling basis

The process:

We are glad you’re interested in applying for this role!

After each step, we decide whether to invite you to the next one. The screening process takes approximately 4–6 weeks from the application deadline and includes the following stages:

  1. CV screening
  2. Data test
  3. First-round interview
  4. Second-round interview

Depending on the candidate pool, we may add any additional interviews to make a well thought through decision.

Our commitment to diversity:

GBL is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, age, physical disability, or length of time spent unemployed. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We are a young and growing company making us the ideal ground for team members to experiment, take on dynamic roles, and grow with us. We focus on happiness, output, and quality of work.

If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know during the recruiting process.

Salary: $80,000–$100,000 annually, subject to the candidate’s experience, skills, and fit for the role.

title: Port Captain
description:
The Port Captain is responsible for the planning, coordination, oversight, and execution of vessel and cargo operations within assigned ports, ensuring activities are conducted safely, efficiently, and in alignment with operational, commercial, and customer objectives. Serving as a key operational representative of the Company, the Port Captain acts as the primary liaison among vessel owners and operators, steamship lines, terminal operators, stevedores, labor organizations, customers, surveyors, port authorities, and other stakeholders involved in vessel and cargo operations.

Leveraging extensive maritime industry expertise and cargo-handling knowledge, the Port Captain coordinates port calls, monitors vessel performance, resolves operational challenges, and drives continuous improvement in vessel and terminal operations. The Port Captain exercises independent judgment and discretion in planning vessel operations, evaluating operational risks, allocating resources, resolving complex operational issues, and recommending and implementing operational adjustments, where authorized, that impact operational efficiency, customer service, safety performance, regulatory compliance, cost management, and overall business results. Acting as the Company's designated operational representative, the Port Captain is responsible for making real-time operational decisions necessary to support safe, compliant, and efficient vessel and cargo operations while balancing customer requirements, operational constraints, and commercial objectives.

This role requires the ability to effectively manage multiple stakeholders, maintain regulatory and safety compliance, and support the successful execution of customer requirements. Depending on operational needs, vessel schedules, cargo types, and port activities, the Port Captain may be required to work both onsite at marine terminals and aboard vessels, as well as remotely coordinate and oversee operations across multiple locations.

Specific Essential Job Duties

Vessel and Cargo Operations / Cargo Planning and Documentation

  • Plan, coordinate, and oversee vessel and cargo operations to ensure the safe, efficient, and timely execution of loading, discharge, and vessel turnaround activities.
  • Develop and manage cargo stowage, loading, and discharge plans while optimizing vessel utilization, operational performance, and customer service.
  • Coordinate with vessel personnel, terminal operators, stevedores, customers, and other stakeholders to support seamless cargo movement and operational execution.
  • Monitor production, vessel schedules, labor utilization, cargo volumes, and operational performance, implementing solutions to address delays, improve efficiency, and achieve operational objectives.
  • Review, maintain, and reconcile cargo manifests, operational records, and planning documentation to ensure accuracy, compliance, and effective operational reporting.
  • Evaluate operational requirements and recommend adjustments to labor, equipment, work processes, and cargo plans to maximize productivity, control costs, and support successful vessel operations.
  • Exercise independent judgment in evaluating operational alternatives, prioritizing resources, and implementing or recommending solutions to address vessel, cargo, labor, equipment, scheduling, and service-related challenges.
  • Maintain accurate operational data, reports, and documentation while supporting continuous improvement in cargo planning, reporting, and vessel operations.

Labor, Stevedore, and Customer Relations

  • Build and maintain effective working relationships with terminal operators, stevedores, labor representatives, customers, vessel owners, steamship lines, and other key stakeholders to support successful vessel and cargo operations.
  • Coordinate labor resources and operational requirements to ensure safe, efficient, and cost-effective execution of cargo handling activities.
  • Monitor workforce productivity, operational performance, and resource utilization, recommending adjustments to staffing, equipment, and work processes as needed.
  • Communicate operational objectives, vessel schedules, production performance, and service expectations to internal and external stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with labor and business partners to resolve operational issues, delays, claims, and customer concerns while maintaining positive working relationships.
  • Serve as a primary operational contact, ensuring timely communication, strong customer service, and effective execution of customer and vessel operator requirements.
  • Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency, stakeholder satisfaction, service quality, and overall business performance.

Port, Vessel, and Operational Coordination

  • Coordinate vessel, cargo, and terminal operations across assigned ports to ensure safe, efficient, and compliant execution of operational activities.
  • Maintain effective working relationships with port authorities, terminal operators, vessel personnel, marine service providers, customers, and other key stakeholders.
  • Conduct vessel attendance, operational inspections, and site visits to monitor cargo handling, vessel readiness, operational performance, and compliance with Company and customer requirements.
  • Monitor and manage vessel schedules, cargo movements, operational progress, and performance metrics, both onsite and remotely, across multiple locations.
  • Identify, document, and communicate operational issues, cargo exceptions, delays, and risks, while implementing solutions to minimize disruptions.
  • Prepare operational reports, inspection documentation, and status updates, providing timely communication and recommendations to management and stakeholders.
  • Support operational improvement initiatives, maintain compliance with applicable port and terminal requirements, and represent the Company professionally in all external interactions.

Reporting and Operational Analysis

  • Prepare, analyze, and maintain operational reports, records, forecasts, and performance metrics related to vessel operations, cargo activity, labor utilization, productivity, and schedule performance.
  • Monitor operational trends, evaluate operational and business impacts, identify areas for improvement, and develop recommendations that influence operational efficiency, customer service, cost management, labor utilization, and overall business performance.
  • Develop and maintain tracking tools, schedules, dashboards, and analytical reports using Excel and other business systems to support operational planning and decision-making.
  • Provide operational analysis, planning recommendations, forecasting support, productivity assessments, and business improvement recommendations to management in support of strategic and operational objectives.

Safety

  • Monitor and track safety key performance indicators (KPIs) and training compliance.
  • Organize and lead safety meetings to promote awareness and best practices.
  • Ensure adherence to company safety policies and regulations.
  • Prepare and submit safety reports as required.
  • Develop and implement standard operating procedures and guidelines to maintain a safe and environmentally responsible work environment.
  • Ensure all personnel complete and comply with mandatory regulatory training requirements.
  • Maintain a professional office environment, ensuring it is well-prepared for visits from colleagues, customers, government officials, stevedores, port managers and other visitors.
  • Support and enforce the NLI safety program, ensuring full compliance with all federal, state, and local regulations. Ensure proper safety gear is available to all team members.

Misc.

  • Abide by company HSEQ policies and procedures.
  • This job description is not exhaustive; additional duties may be assigned as needed. This role may evolve in response to changes in industry practices and technological advancements.

Qualifications & Requirements

Education / Experience:

  • High school diploma or GED required; bachelor’s degree in Business, Maritime Studies, or a related field is preferred.
  • Relevant experience in the maritime or port services industry is preferred.
  • A combination of relevant education (e.g., degree, certifications) and hands-on experience is preferred.
  • ASBA Agency Certification required or must be obtained within six (6) months of hire.

Competencies:

  • Demonstrated customer service skills with a focus on responsiveness, professionalism, and solution-oriented support.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Outlook, Word, Excel) and other business software, with the ability to quickly learn and adapt to new technologies and systems.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate professionally across all organizational levels, departments, and both in-office and remote teams, while effectively supporting local and port office operations.
  • Works effectively independently or as part of a team.
  • Proven ability to plan, prioritize, and manage multiple concurrent tasks in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Able to quickly adjust to shifting priorities and changing demands, delivering both short-term operational results and longer-term initiatives.
  • Self-directed and accountable, demonstrating strong problem-solving skills and a results-driven mindset under pressure.

Additional Requirements:

  • Must possess and maintain a valid driver’s license with an acceptable motor vehicle record (MVR).
  • Must have reliable transportation and maintain automobile insurance in accordance with state requirements.
  • Must possess or be able to obtain a Transportation Worker Identification Credential (TWIC) within ninety (90) days of hire and maintain it throughout employment.
  • Ability to safely board vessels using gangways, ladders, or launches.
  • Ability to work in variable weather conditions and dynamic port environments.
  • Must be available to work a flexible schedule based on business needs, including days, nights, weekends, and some holidays with travel to and from the marine vessel while in Port.

Working Conditions


  • This position involves a combination of office-based work and shipboard duties, which includes time aboard vessels at a dock or moored/anchored location or position.
  • While in the office, work is typically performed in a climate-controlled environment with standard office equipment.
  • While aboard vessels, employees may be exposed to varying weather conditions, confined spaces, moving machinery, and potentially hazardous materials.
  • May require climbing ladders, walking on uneven or slippery surfaces, and working in elevated or enclosed areas.
  • Must be able to lift and carry equipment or supplies up to 50 pounds as needed.
  • Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), including but not limited to hard hats, safety footwear, gloves, and life vests, must be worn as required by company policy, port / terminal requirements, and maritime regulations. The required PPE will be organized by your supervisor.
  • Compliance with all maritime safety regulations—including U.S. Coast Guard, OSHA, and company protocols—is required. Participation in safety drills, emergency response training, and regular safety briefings are mandatory.
