title: Consultant: Tax and Non-Tax Incentives for Mining Downstream Viability Projects:
description:
The International Institute for Sustainable Development is a globally recognized think tank with more than 30 years of experience working to solve today's greatest sustainable development challenges. We combine deep expertise across critical policy areas with a collaborative approach to research, advice, and hands-on support that delivers real-world results. Headquartered in Winnipeg, Manitoba, we are a diverse team of over 300 experts working from offices in Canada and Switzerland as well as other locations around the world.

IISD hosts the Secretariat of the Intergovernmental Forum on Mining, Minerals, Metals and Sustainable Development (IGF).

The IGF's Global Mining Tax Initiative (GMTI) helps countries to increase mining revenues for sustainable development. Drawing on broad experience working with IGF member governments, the Secretariat offers this specialized and comprehensive program covering fiscal policy for the entire mining value chain, from exploration and development to mining, processing, mineral sales, and mine closure. The GMTI focuses on all aspects of fiscal policy, including taxes, royalties, and financial modelling, and has developed particular expertise on the fiscal treatment of mineral beneficiation and downstream processing.

The Challenge

As demand for critical minerals accelerates with the energy transition, a growing number of resource-rich countries are moving to capture more of the value chain domestically and attract investment. Whilst a variety of fiscal and non-fiscal tools are available, many resource-rich countries offer tax and non-tax incentives to attract investment into downstream mineral processing, from smelting and refining to further stages of value addition. These incentives can include corporate income tax holidays, accelerated depreciation, royalty relief, value-added tax and import duty exemptions, energy subsidies, infrastructure provision, export restrictions or differentiated export taxes on unprocessed ore, and guaranteed offtake arrangements.

Governments introduce these measures with the aim of capturing more value domestically, creating jobs, and building industrial capacity. However, the fiscal and non-fiscal cost of these incentives is rarely tracked systematically, and there is limited evidence on whether they actually influence investment decisions or simply reward projects that would have gone ahead regardless. Downstream processing economics are also heavily shaped by global market conditions, such as smelting overcapacity and depressed treatment and refining charges, that incentives alone cannot offset. Governments are often left weighing significant revenue foregone against uncertain and long-dated returns in jobs, value addition, and industrial development.

Our Response

To help governments make better-informed decisions on this trade-off, the IGF is developing a practice note assessing the short-, medium-, and long-term impact of tax incentives for mining downstream viability projects. The note will examine three country cases, each anchored to the critical mineral most relevant to its downstream ambitions: Zambia and copper, Brazil and iron ore or niobium, and Guinea and bauxite. Each case will be given equal depth, applying a shared analytical framework so that findings can be compared across countries with materially different fiscal capacity, market structure, and governance context.

Deliverable – Technical Input for the Downstream Incentives Practice Note

The IGF seeks a consultant, or small consultant team, to research and support the drafting of the comparative practice note. The consultant will be responsible for the following tasks:

  1. Prepare a short inception note confirming, for each of the three countries, the downstream stage under review (for example, smelting and refining for copper, alumina and possible smelter-grade aluminium for bauxite, and pelletizing, direct reduced iron, or ferroniobium processing for iron ore and niobium), the incentive taxonomy to be applied consistently across cases, and the impact metrics and time horizons to be used.
  2. For each of the three countries, document the incentives each received or was eligible for and assess the role those incentives played in the project's outcome relative to other determinants.
    1. Inventory and governance: For each of the three countries, compile an inventory of tax and non-tax incentives from the mining code, tax legislation, investment and industrialization laws, and any special economic zone regimes, capturing not just which incentives are available, but how they are governed: their legal basis, the granting authority, eligibility criteria and conditions, and the administrative and monitoring arrangements that shape how effective they are in practice.
    2. Projects: Identify actual downstream projects (built, under construction, planned, or abandoned), documenting the incentives each received or was eligible for and assessing the role those incentives played in the project's outcome relative to other determinants.
  3. Gather available fiscal and economic data for each country, including revenue foregone estimates where they exist, capital investment, employment, and the share of raw versus processed mineral exports over time, and flag data gaps and how they were addressed.
  4. Conduct stakeholder consultations in each country, engaging as relevant the ministry of finance, ministry of mines, revenue authority, investment promotion agency, state mining company, and major private operators.
  5. Draft the practice note, presenting the three country cases in a common format with a synthesis chapter setting out crosscutting findings and being explicit about the limits of comparability between the cases.
  6. Revise the draft in response to internal IGF review and, where relevant, feedback from country authorities.

Timelines

  1. Inception note confirming scope, framework, and metrics for all three countries. Due: November 2026. Days: 3 days.
  2. Literature review and international comparative summary. Due: November 2026. Estimated effort: 5 days.
  3. Incentive inventory and project mapping for Zambia (copper). Due: November 2026. Estimated effort: 3 days.
  4. Incentive inventory and project mapping for Brazil (iron ore/niobium). Due: December 2026. Estimated effort: 3 days.
  5. Incentive inventory and project mapping for Fuinea (bauxite). Due: December 2026. Estimated effort: 3 days.
  6. Preparation of questionnaire for stakeholder consultations. Due: December 2026. Estimated effort: 1 day.
  7. First draft and final draft of report. Due: December 2026. Estimated effort: 18 days.

Location: Remote

IISD will not apply for residency and work permits for this position on behalf of the applicant.

Candidates must hold appropriate work authorization for locations where they expect to be based.

Application Process

Application deadline: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until filled.

This is a consultant position. Submissions must be in English.

To apply for this consultancy, interested applicants should submit the following:

  • A CV (detailing your experience with mining fiscal policy, tax expenditure analysis, or downstream mineral processing).
  • An expression of interest (one page), including proposed approach and, where relevant, coverage of the three countries by team member if submitting as a team.

NOTE:

  • Incomplete applications will be automatically disqualified.
  • Only those candidates IISD wishes to interview will be contacted.

Countybank

  • Learn directly from the Information Security Officer while gaining practical experience across multiple areas of an Information Security Program.
  • Build broad experience through exposure to risk assessments, audits and examinations, access controls, security awareness, business continuity and disaster recovery, and compliance monitoring.
  • Understand the "why" behind the work, including how security controls, policies, processes, and regulatory expectations work together to help protect a financial institution.
  • Develop an enterprise perspective by working across lines of business and departments and seeing how information security intersects with technology, operations, risk, compliance, and the business. The role is designed to coordinate information security activities across departments rather than operate within only one area.
  • Grow your responsibilities over time as your knowledge, judgment, and capabilities develop.

Key Responsibilities

Information Security Program Administration

Support the implementation and ongoing administration of Countybank's approved information security policies, procedures, and standards. Maintain documentation, inventories, and supporting evidence that demonstrate compliance with established practices and controls.

Risk, Audit, and Examination Support

Assist with the execution, documentation, and tracking of information security risk assessments, remediation items, and management responses, as well as audit and examination activities. Organize and maintain supporting documentation and evidence and track follow-up items through completion.

Security Awareness and Training

Coordinate and support information security awareness and training activities with the Information Security Officer and Information Technology Operations Manager, including tracking completion and maintaining training records.

Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery

Coordinate the testing, documentation, and ongoing maintenance of the Information Systems components of Countybank's Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Program under the direction of the Information Security Officer.

Access and Security Controls

Work with Information Technology to support the administration and monitoring of technical and operational controls, including access controls, authentication, logging, and monitoring activities.

User Access Reviews

Coordinate periodic user access reviews, document results, and track necessary remediation in accordance with established policies and procedures.

Compliance Monitoring and Reporting

Monitor adherence to information security policies and procedures and escalate identified issues, exceptions, or potential violations to the Information Security Officer as appropriate. Support operational and metrics-based reporting to the Information Security Officer and Technology Committee as directed.

Internal Partnership

Serve as an internal information security resource and provide subject matter support to managers and associates, as directed by the Information Security Officer, while developing an understanding of how information security requirements apply across different areas of the organization.

What We're Looking For

You don't need to have encountered every aspect of information security to bring valuable experience to this role. Success will depend on how you approach the work, your ability to learn, and your willingness to develop deeper expertise over time.

The person who thrives in this role will:

  • Be able to analyze complex information and connect individual details to larger processes, controls, and risks.
  • Exercise sound judgment and recognize when information or circumstances may require additional review.
  • Value accuracy and understand why documentation, consistent execution, and follow-through matter in a regulated environment.
  • Work effectively within established policies, procedures, and controls while still thinking critically about the information in front of them.
  • Enjoy learning how systems, processes, people, policies, and controls work together.
  • Communicate clearly and work effectively with both technical and nontechnical colleagues.
  • Handle confidential and sensitive information with appropriate judgment and discretion.
  • Be motivated to continue learning as technology, information security risks, and regulatory expectations evolve.

An Opportunity to Learn and Grow

We recognize that someone building a career in information security may not come to Countybank having already encountered every area covered by this position. What matters is having the right foundation, mindset, and motivation to learn.

Through direct work with the Information Security Officer and collaboration with Information Technology and other areas of Countybank, this role offers the opportunity to develop practical experience while gaining an understanding of how an Information Security Program operates within a regulated financial institution. As your knowledge and capabilities grow, so can the complexity of your work and the contribution you make to Countybank's Information Security Program. The breadth of the position includes risk assessments, audit and examination support, information security awareness, business continuity and disaster recovery, technical and operational controls, user access reviews, compliance monitoring, and reporting.

Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's or associate degree in information security, cybersecurity, information technology, business, risk management, or a related field preferred, but not required.

Experience

  • Previous experience in information security, information technology, risk management, audit, compliance, banking operations, internal controls, or a similar role is preferred, but not required.
  • Experience working in a financial institution or other regulated environment is a plus.
  • Experience reviewing information, processes, controls, documentation, or data for accuracy and identifying items that require follow-up or further review is beneficial.

Knowledge and Skills

  • Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to analyze information, identify inconsistencies or potential concerns, and determine when additional review may be appropriate.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage detailed information and follow items through to completion.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with both technical and nontechnical audiences.
  • Ability to understand and work within established policies, procedures, standards, and controls.
  • Sound judgment and discretion when handling confidential, sensitive, or security-related information.
  • Ability to learn new systems, technologies, processes, and technical concepts.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across departments and build productive working relationships.
  • Commitment to continued learning and professional development.

This is a full-time position in a smoke- and drug-free workplace with strong corporate values that foster associate growth and satisfaction.

Why Countybank?

Countybank combines the stability of a well-established financial institution with the entrepreneurial spirit of a growing organization. Since 1933, we have built our reputation on trusted relationships, sound financial stewardship, and a commitment to serving our customers, associates, shareholders, and communities.

With approximately $740 million in assets and a diversified financial services model that extends beyond traditional banking, Countybank offers a unique opportunity for finance professionals seeking broad exposure, meaningful influence, and long-term professional growth.

If you're looking for an opportunity to broaden your financial leadership experience, influence strategy, and help shape the future of a growing financial services organization, we would welcome the opportunity to learn more about you.

title: Systems Engineer - Aerospace
description:

title: Branch Manager
description:
Working for Pacific Service Credit Union

We put people first. That includes our members, our employees and the communities we serve. We hire energetic and enthusiastic people who want to work as part of our team.

What’s in it for you?

Health insurance coverage: We provide our employees with 100% premium employer-paid medical, dental, vision, disability and basic life insurance for full-time employees and a low monthly premium for eligible dependents.

401k: We contribute 3% of your base salary to your 401k account regardless of whether you contribute or not. In addition, we match 75% of your contributions up to the first 3% of eligible compensation beginning after your first day of employment and up to 6% after three years of service.

Bonus program: All employees are rewarded for attaining our annual organizational goals.

Tuition Reimbursement program for employees eligible after six months of service.

Recognition program where employees can be nominated by management, their peers or by members.

Employee referral bonus.

Student Loan Repayment Assistance: Contributions toward your student loans every month by the credit union after six months of service.

Employees are eligible to receive a consumer loan rate discount

Vacation and sick time: Full-time employees receive more than two weeks’ vacation per year, 11 paid holidays and 10 days of sick leave.


Our Hiring Process

We believe it’s important for you to know where you stand in our hiring process. Below is an outline of the steps we take to make the best hires possible.

Apply: Submit your resume for one of our job openings.

Our Talent Team and our partner – Total Quality Consulting (TQC Team) will review your submitted information and will call or email successful applicants for an interview as soon as possible.

In-Person Interview: After a screening call with TQC, we’ll invite a final number of candidates to our office for an in-person interview or set up a live Zoom meeting with the hiring manager(s).

If we believe that you have what it takes, we'll make an offer and provide next steps in the hiring process!


About this Role

At Pacific Service Credit Union, we are committed to strategic growth through trust, innovation, and operational excellence. By empowering our internal teams with the tools and support they need to succeed, we strengthen organizational efficiency, ensure compliance, and advance our mission of enhancing member financial well-being.

The Branch Manager is responsible for managing and executing branch strategy and daily operations to drive local market growth while delivering exceptional, member-focused service. The role guides, coaches, and supports branch staff to maintain high service standards, achieve performance goals, and continuously improve through training, feedback, and professional development. This position manages operational integrity by monitoring compliance, audit readiness, cash controls, and regulatory requirements, while delivering complex transactions, loan origination, and fraud support. The Branch Manager coordinates business and community development efforts, serves as a brand ambassador, and builds lasting relationships with members and internal partners. Through ongoing evaluation and implementation of process improvements and technology, the role tracks performance and improves efficiency, service quality, and the overall member experience.

This role requires a hands-on leader with strong organizational and communication skills, and a proven ability to deliver results through effective planning, prioritization and effective execution. The position supports the organization’s goals by managing day-to-day operations, coaching and developing staff, supporting strategic initiatives, and driving positive member/service outcomes.


Essential Job Functions

• Manage staffing responsibilities, including hiring, training, cross-training, counseling, performance evaluation, and discipline of all department personnel.

• Directly manage a team of branch employees by providing day-to-day leadership, coaching, and performance management to deliver exceptional service across all member communication channels.

• Develop and execute strategies to drive credit union growth in the local market.

• Guide team members by leading through example to ensure professional, timely, accurate, and engaging interactions with members and prospective members.

• Drive a performance- and culture-focused department by analyzing members needs, aligningsolutions with products and services, consistently meeting or exceeding branch goals.

• Lead and support team members through change, resolving high pressure situations with professionalism, tact, and emotional intelligence.

• Strong ability to build lasting relationships with members and PSCU employees through effective communication, interpersonal skills, and trust.

• Support team member career development through ongoing coaching, feedback, and professional development.

• Serve as a brand ambassador in the local market, leading and supporting business and community development initiatives, including community and corporate events.

• Deliver exceptional service while assisting members and non-members with banking transactions,withdrawals, transfers, payments, account maintenance, and fraud assistance.

• Conduct thorough needs assessments and manages the processing and funding of loan applications for new and existing members, in compliance with NMLS requirements.

• Independently handle and resolve escalated member concerns with discretion, diplomacy, and sound judgement in complex and sensitive situations.

• Maintain expert-level knowledge of the credit union’s products and services, to including complex account types such as Trusts, POAs, IRAs, and other fiduciary accounts.

• Manage tasks related to Audit Checklist, as well as all daily, monthly and quarterly responsibilities to contribute to a successful audit.

• Perform reconciliation and balancing of the Vault, Cash Recycler, ATM, and individual cash drawer.

• Recommend and implement process improvements, using data-driven insights and evolving technology to improve efficiency and member experience.

• Mentor and coach team fostering a culture of high performance, continuous improvement and professional growth in accordance with the credit union's performance management philosophy.

• Set clear goals and objectives for team members, providing regular feedback and performance evaluations.

• Support and participate in enterprise-wide initiatives, including product development and enhancement, cost optimization, and process improvement efforts designed to increase efficiency, streamline operations, and ensure organizational relevance.

• Assist with the creation and implementation of the annual plan and budget.

• Take ownership of responsibilities, sets clear objectives, delivers results, and follows through on commitments. Model integrity and professionalism, reinforcing trust, discipline, and operational excellence within the team.

• Ensure compliance with a variety of internal policies and procedures.

• Comply with all anti-money laundering laws, including the Bank Secrecy Act, OFAC regulations, and the USA PATRIOT Act, as well as all related policies and procedures.

• Demonstrate dependable performance including attendance and punctuality, recognizing that it is essential to organizational excellence and operational success.

Supporting Functions

• Provide back-up and support to VP, as directed.

• Performs special projects and other responsibilities, as directed.


Competencies

The following competencies are essential for success in this role:

Drives vision and strategy: Understands organizational objectives and translates them into actionable team initiatives. Connects short-term tasks to longer-term goals to support growth, operational efficiency, and department performance.

Prioritizes and organizes work: Efficiently manages tasks and resources, focuses on key objectives, anticipates needs, and balances multiple priorities under time constraints.

Drives outcomes: Makes timely decisions, takes calculated risks, acts decisively, overcomes obstacles, and drives initiatives to successful completion.

Emotional intelligence: Demonstrates self-awareness, adapts interpersonal style to context, regulates emotions, and interacts with empathy and respect.

Builds talent: Recruits and retains talent, guides and cultivates employees, aligns strengths with opportunities, identifies and develops potential and creates a career-growth environment.

Manages ambiguity: Effectively works with incomplete information, adapts to evolving circumstances, applies critical thinking and remains resilient under changing conditions.

Team leadership: Drives collective success through effective teamwork and collaboration, leverages team strengths, meets commitments, and fosters collaboration to achieve shared goals.

Delegation: Clarifies expectations, enables ownership, assigns appropriately challenging tasks and equips employees with the tools and guidance needed for success.

Change management: Actively supports initiatives, guides teams through transitions, models adaptability and embraces change to achieve positive outcomes.


Required Minimum Qualifications

Education:

• High School diploma or equivalent, required.

• College degree in business, marketing, sales, or other related business discipline, preferred.

Experience:

• Minimum three (3) years within a supervisory role at a credit union, bank, or related field, required.

• Proven experience coaching and developing individual employees and teams to success.

• Demonstrated business and community development experience, including serving as a brand ambassador at local businesses and community events, and prospecting new business partnerships.

• Self-starter with the ability to manage projects independently, follow through to completion, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

• Proven experience managing cross-functional projects.

• Confident and effective in delivering presentations to both large and small groups.

• Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to communicate clearly and professionally with employees, members, and executive leadership in person, via phone or email.

• Proven ability to handle and resolve difficult or escalated situations with professionalism and tact.

• Solid knowledge of credit union operations, products and services, policies, and applicable regulatory requirements.

• Experience representing an organization or brand in the community and with business partners, including sourcing and cultivating new business relationships.

• Experience leading diverse work teams, required.

• Excellent oral and written communication skills required.

• Must be proficient in computer programs (e.g., Microsoft Office Suite).

Preferred Qualifications

• Knowledge of Symitar software system, preferred.


Physical Requirements

Hearing: Ability to hear and comprehend spoken communication in person and over the phone.

Vision: Ability to view computer screens and read documentation with clarity and accuracy.

Verbal Communication: Ability to speak clearly and effectively to interact with colleagues and/or members. Frequent use of telephone headset may be required.

Manual Dexterity: Proficient use of hands and fingers for typing, operating office equipment, and handling documents.

Posture and Endurance: Ability to sit or stand at a workstation for extended periods; adjustable sit/stand desk options may be available to support comfort.

Mobility: Ability to move within the office environment to attend meetings or assist colleagues, as needed.

Lifting and Carrying: Occasionally required to lift and carry materials weighing up to 30 lbs.


Other Information

Hours Required: This position requires working standard branch hours, Monday through Friday. Work hours and branch locations may vary based on business needs and business development activities. This position is not eligible for telecommuting.

The typical schedule is Monday through Thursday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., and Friday, an eight-hour shift scheduled between 8:30 a.m. and 6:30 p.m.

Travel Requirements: Less than 50% local travel required. Limited travel during the work schedule, primarily for training, meetings, or special projects.

Work Environment: This position is based on climate-controlled professional, indoor branch environment with ergonomic workstations and frequent face-to-face member interaction. The role involves regular use of computers, phones, and standard office equipment in a moderate-noise, service-oriented setting and requires adherence to all security, confidentiality, and regulatory requirements. Natural light from large windows, supplemented by artificial lighting to ensure a comfortable working atmosphere.


Disclaimer

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change, or new ones may be assigned at any time with or without notice.

title: Senior Radar Engineer
description:

title: Director, Strategic Partnerships & Scouting
description:
The Director, Strategic Partnerships & Scouting will support the company’s worldwide efforts to strategically advance the Dechra portfolio. title: IT Operations & Cybersecurity Specialist
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an IT Operations & Cybersecurity Specialist based in Austria.

Join a distributed technology team dedicated to delivering reliable IT operations and strengthening cybersecurity for organisations that handle sensitive data. In this remote, hands-on role, you will manage day-to-day IT administration, support users, and maintain secure digital environments for multiple clients. You will work with modern cloud productivity platforms, endpoint management tools, and automation technologies to ensure systems remain secure, compliant, and operational. Beyond routine IT support, you will contribute to security initiatives involving vulnerability research, device hardening, and incident response documentation. This position offers an opportunity to develop your cybersecurity expertise while taking ownership of operational responsibilities. You will thrive in an autonomous, asynchronous working environment that values reliability, continuous learning, and practical problem-solving.

Accountabilities

  • IT Administration: Provision and manage user accounts, groups, permissions, and licences across Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, ensuring secure and efficient access to business applications.
  • Endpoint Management: Prepare and onboard Windows and macOS laptops into mobile device management (MDM) platforms, coordinate remote device handovers, and maintain appropriate device configurations.
  • Technical Support: Handle first-line support requests, including password resets, access issues, and routine troubleshooting, while escalating more complex incidents when necessary.
  • IT Maintenance and Monitoring: Conduct weekly maintenance checks covering software patch status, backup logs, security alerts, and general system health to help maintain reliable operations.
  • Documentation and Process Improvement: Document technical fixes, standard operating procedures, and runbooks to improve consistency, knowledge sharing, and operational efficiency.
  • Cybersecurity Projects: Dedicate approximately 20% of your time to security-focused initiatives, including CVE research and briefings, laptop hardening scripts, incident-response playbooks, and ISO 27001 checklist development.
  • Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities to streamline IT workflows, strengthen security practices, and improve service delivery across a distributed client environment.

Requirements

  • Professional Experience: At least two years of hands-on experience in IT operations, helpdesk support, systems administration, or a comparable technical role.
  • Cloud Administration: Practical experience administering Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, including user and group management, security policies, permissions, and basic troubleshooting.
  • Endpoint Management: Familiarity with MDM solutions such as Microsoft Intune, Jamf, or equivalent platforms, including device enrolment and configuration.
  • Scripting and Automation: Proficiency in at least one scripting language, such as PowerShell, Bash, or Python, with the ability to automate routine tasks and improve operational workflows.
  • Communication Skills: Strong written and spoken English, with the ability to document technical processes clearly and collaborate effectively with distributed teams. German language skills are an advantage.
  • Remote Working Readiness: A reliable internet connection, a professional remote working environment, and the ability to work independently across different time zones.
  • Personal Attributes: A proactive, organised, and detail-oriented approach, with strong troubleshooting skills, sound judgement, and a willingness to learn and take ownership of responsibilities.
  • Preferred Qualifications: Microsoft 365 Administrator Expert, Microsoft 365 Endpoint Administrator, or Google Workspace Administrator certifications are advantageous.
  • Security Knowledge: Exposure to cybersecurity and compliance frameworks such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, or similar standards is a plus.

title: Claims Examiner III (Medi-Cal Managed Care)
description:
We are seeking an experienced Senior Claims Examiner with deep expertise in Medi-Cal Managed Care claims adjudication. The ideal candidate will have extensive knowledge of California Medi-Cal regulations, delegated risk arrangements, provider disputes, and complex facility claim processing. Experience with Medicare and Commercial claims is required, but this role is primarily focused on supporting and serving as a subject matter expert for Medi-Cal business.

About Us

All Care To You is a Management Service Organization providing our clients with healthcare administrative support. We provide services to Independent Physician Associations, TPAs, and Fiscal Intermediary clients. ACTY is a modern growing company which encourages diverse perspectives. We celebrate curiosity, initiative, drive and a passion for making a difference. We support a culture focused on teamwork, support, and inclusion. Our company is fully remote and offers a flexible work environment as well as schedules. ACTY offers 100% employer paid medical, vision, dental, and life coverage for our employees. We also offer paid holiday, sick time, and vacation time as well as a 401k plan. Additional employee paid coverage options available.

Job Purpose

The Claims Examiner III (Medi-Cal Managed Care) is responsible for the accurate processing, adjustment, adjudication, and release of complex hospital, ancillary, and professional claims with a primary focus on Medi-Cal managed care claims. This role requires extensive knowledge of California Medi-Cal regulations, delegated IPA and capitated hospital arrangements, provider disputes, and claims payment requirements.

The ideal candidate is a subject matter expert in Medi-Cal claims processing and is also experienced in Medicare and Commercial lines of business. This individual will identify claim processing issues, perform root cause analysis, recommend operational improvements, support compliance initiatives, and ensure adherence to CMS, DHCS, DMHC, and applicable state regulations. The Claims Examiner III must consistently meet production and quality standards while serving as a resource to other team members.

Duties and responsibilities

  • Process, adjust, and adjudicate professional, institutional, and complex claims with a primary focus on Medi-Cal Managed Care, while supporting Medicare and Commercial lines of business.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert for Medi-Cal claims processing, reimbursement methodologies, delegated risk arrangements, and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Review and apply provider contracts, benefit plans, divisions of financial responsibility, authorizations, and reimbursement methodologies to ensure accurate claim adjudication.
  • Validate diagnosis and procedure codes and ensure claims are processed in accordance with DHCS, DMHC, CMS, AB 1455, AB 1324, and other applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Research, analyze, and resolve complex claims issues, payment discrepancies, provider disputes, grievances, escalations, and claims processing errors.
  • Process claim adjustments, voids, reopenings, reconsiderations, overpayment recoveries, and underpayment corrections in accordance with departmental guidelines.
  • Generate and document provider communications, including acknowledgement, development, denial, resolution, and notification letters as required.
  • Collaborate with Customer Service, Provider Relations, Configuration, Compliance, and other departments to resolve claims and payment issues.
  • Create and utilize Crystal and SQL reports to support inventory management, operational efficiency, and regulatory turnaround time compliance.
  • Identify claims payment errors, system configuration issues, and process improvement opportunities; provide recommendations for corrective action.
  • Participate in internal and external audits, regulatory reviews, workflow improvement initiatives, and special projects.
  • Meet established productivity and quality standards while maintaining accurate documentation within EZ-Cap and related systems.
  • May assist with training, mentoring, check run preparation, and other departmental needs as assigned.
  • Comply with all company policies, procedures, and confidentiality requirements.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of claims adjudication experience with significant experience processing Medi-Cal managed care claims.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience processing Medicare and Commercial claims.
  • Experience using EZ-Cap required.
  • Extensive knowledge of California Medi-Cal, Medicare, and Commercial reimbursement methodologies.
  • Thorough understanding of DHCS, DMHC, CMS, and applicable state and federal claims regulations.
  • Experience with delegated IPA, Medical Group, and capitated provider arrangements.
  • Demonstrated experience resolving Provider Disputes (PDRs), claims appeals, grievances, and escalated claims issues.
  • Strong understanding of:
  • AB 1455 Claims Settlement Practices
  • AB 1324 Requirements
  • Knox-Keene regulations
  • Timely filing requirements
  • Coordination of Benefits (COB)
  • Claims payment and regulatory turnaround requirements
  • Knowledge of CPT, HCPCS, ICD-10, DRG, APC, ASC, and other reimbursement methodologies.
  • Proficient in outpatient PPS, inpatient DRG, interim rate payment methodologies, and other reimbursement structures applicable to Medi-Cal, Medicare, and Commercial products.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and claims research skills

Working conditions

  • This job may require flexible work hours due to the nature of the responsibilities.

Physical requirements

  • This job is not considered physically demanding, therefore there are no physical requirements.
Salary: $28.00 - $35.00 hourly ($75,000 Annually)

description:

The values we exhibit as an organization show the strength of our staff, our leadership and our community. We expect all employees to exhibit LifeLine’s core values as we complete daily tasks, provide services to clients and care for our animals.


The Transport Coordinator is integral in helping to transport animals between Fulton County Animal Services for placement needs and medical care, etc., as well as helping to transport pets of families with no transportation back to their homes.

Essential Job Functions:

This represents a list of essential job duties. Other duties or special projects may be assigned as needed.

Save Lives -- Build Community -- Be Exceptional Stewards -- Be Courageous --

Be Compassionate -- Take Responsibility -- Respect, Embrace and Celebrate Diversity

23 years of age or older required for the purposes of being added to group vehicle insurance policy.

About the Role

Reporting into the Manager, Dealer Implementations, the Implementations Configuration Specialist is responsible for the accurate, timely configuration and integration of AutoFi's products to support successful Dealer Partner launches, including new implementations and product expansions for existing partners. In this role, you will work closely with Dealer Onboarding Specialists, internal stakeholders, and third-party vendors, translate Dealer Partner requirements into functional technical configurations, troubleshoot issues, and ensure assigned deliverables meet established quality standards and launch timelines.

Implementation Services is devoted to receiving and caring for net-new Dealer Partners as well as product upsells to existing Dealer Partners that originate through the Sales organization. They work with Dealers and their representatives to ensure that all aspects of their Program with AutoFi are appropriately configured for a successful launch, from basic configurations/feature enablement all the way through to complex integrations and related testing. They are subject matter experts with a deep understanding of how to use, speak to and configure AutoFi’s product suite to best meet our Dealer Partner’s requirements.

An ideal candidate will have strong technical aptitude, attention to detail, independent problem-solving, and the ability to manage a high volume of concurrent implementations with competing priorities. You will take ownership of your work from initial configuration through testing, launch readiness, and completion of required post-launch activities. As part of Implementation Services, you will develop deep expertise in AutoFi's product suite and integrations, helping ensure Dealer Partners are configured to successfully adopt and use our solutions.

Responsibilities

  • Participate in and contribute to a collaborative, accountable team environment with a culture of open communication through knowledge sharing, constructive feedback, and a willingness to support shared priorities.
  • Own the technical configuration and integration of AutoFi's products for assigned Dealer Partner implementations, ensuring requirements are accurately translated into functional, launch-ready solutions.
  • Manage a concurrent workload of approximately 13–20 implementations, effectively balancing competing priorities, dependencies, and deadlines to meet committed launch timelines.
  • Collaborate with Dealer Onboarding Specialists and internal stakeholders to establish achievable launch timelines, identify dependencies, and ensure assigned configuration and integration activities are completed on schedule.
  • Serve as a technical point of contact for Dealer Partners, their representatives, and third-party vendors to gather requirements, provide configuration guidance, troubleshoot issues, and resolve implementation blockers.
  • Manage assigned technical implementation needs through resolution, maintaining accurate case documentation, clear stakeholder communication, and timely follow-up through phone, email and text, leveraging specific internal and vendor communications platforms where applicable.
  • Apply and validate product configurations and integrations using APIs, JSON, XML, HTML, CSS, and other relevant technologies to meet Dealer Partner requirements.
  • Independently review and test completed configurations and integrations for accuracy, completeness, and expected functionality before transitioning work to dedicated Quality Assurance (QA) resources for formal validation.
  • Perform initial troubleshooting of configuration and integration issues, identifying potential root causes, implementing appropriate corrections, and escalating more complex issues when necessary.
  • Partner with QA resources to investigate and resolve identified defects, ensuring outstanding issues are addressed and configurations meet established launch-readiness requirements.
  • Proactively communicate implementation progress, risks, delays, and capacity constraints, escalating concerns early and taking ownership of assigned deliverables through completion.
  • Complete required post-launch configuration adjustments, troubleshooting, documentation, and other follow-up activities accurately and within established timelines.
  • Develop and maintain proficiency in AutoFi's product suite, integration capabilities, and Dealer Partner use cases, providing informed recommendations to optimize program configurations and functionality.
  • Maintain accurate implementation records, configuration specifications, and testing documentation while contributing to process improvements, repeatable best practices, and a collaborative team environment.

Qualifications

  • 2-3 years of experience working with SaaS platforms, technical configurations, system integrations, or related implementation activities.
  • 2-3 years of experience in client-facing implementations, technical onboarding, or SaaS support strongly preferred.
  • Working knowledge of APIs, JSON, XML, HTML, CSS, and Regex strongly preferred
    Hands-on experience using API testing tools, such as Postman, to send requests, validate responses, and investigate integration issues.
  • Technical aptitude and comfort working with software configurations, system settings, integrated applications and AI Agents
    Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality, with demonstrated ability to review and validate work for accuracy, completeness, and expected functionality.
  • Excellent organizational, time management, and prioritization skills, with demonstrated ability to manage a high volume of concurrent assignments and competing deadlines.
  • Ability to contribute to realistic implementation timelines, identify risks and dependencies, and consistently deliver on commitments.
  • Strong ownership and accountability, with the ability to work independently, proactively communicate progress and challenges, and recognize when escalation or additional support is required.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to gather requirements, explain technical concepts, and collaborate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Ability to adapt to changing priorities and requirements while maintaining accuracy, productivity, and a high standard of work.
  • Experience working with third-party integrations, external vendors, or cross-functional implementation teams preferred.
    Familiarity with automotive dealership operations, business models, and technology ecosystems is an asset, but not required.

title: IT Operations & Cybersecurity Specialist

You will work with modern cloud productivity platforms, endpoint management tools, and automation technologies to ensure systems remain secure, compliant, and operational. Beyond routine IT support, you will contribute to security initiatives involving vulnerability research, device hardening, and incident response documentation. This position offers an opportunity to develop your cybersecurity expertise while taking ownership of operational responsibilities. You will thrive in an autonomous, asynchronous working environment that values reliability, continuous learning, and practical problem-solving.

title: Software Intern
description:
Join the Future of Robotic Biomanufacturing!
Multiply Labs is a robotics company on a mission to solve a significant bottleneck in modern medicine: the manufacturing of life-saving advanced biologics - including cell therapies, gene therapies, mRNA therapies, and more.
Currently, advanced biological therapies are produced through manual, labor-intensive processes. This keeps costs astronomical—often exceeding $$2M per patient—and limits access to only a fraction of those in need.
As labor scarcity for scientists compound against increased product complexity and sky-high costs of failure, the emergence of robotics and AI makes the automated manufacturing of biologics feasible, reliable, and economically scalable.
We envision that the biomanufacturing factory of the future is fully robotic - closed, automated, and scalable, making therapeutics for some of the most important indications for patients today widely accessible.
Why This Matters
We don’t just build robots; we build the infrastructure for the next generation of biologics manufacturing. Our technology allows biopharma companies to scale production without redesigning their science, drastically lowering regulatory hurdles and bringing costs down to a level where these treatments can actually reach patients.
The Stack & The Scale
The Mission: Build the world’s best robots to make life-saving therapies accessible to all.
The Technology: Advanced robotic orchestration, high-precision automation, cloud-integrated hardware-software systems, dextrous manipulation, and imitation learning.
The Location: Headquartered in San Francisco, CA.
The Backing: Supported by premier investors, including Casdin Capital, Lux Capital, and Y Combinator.
About the Role
We are looking for Software Engineering Interns to join a highly collaborative team to deliver production ready software that will shape the future of personalized medicine and cell therapy manufacturing systems. This role is for you if you are a strong problem solver, motivated and hard-working student, and excited to experience what it’s like being an engineer at an early-stage startup.

Responsibilities include:

  • Design, build, deploy, troubleshoot and maintain high-quality software that manages the state and coordination of a multi-robot cluster.
  • Build fast, discrete-event simulation tests to validate scheduling logic and throughput assumptions before code hits physical hardware.
  • Collaborate with team members in implementing and testing scheduling logic for multi-agent workflows.
  • Help develop and maintain tools to intelligently manage shared resources across parallel manufacturing batches.
  • Work on developing and monitoring the connectivity tooling between on-premise robots and AWS.
  • Contribute to the automated test suite, focusing on improving test coverage for non-deterministic robotic behaviors and streamlining the integration process.
  • Participate in code reviews, document system architectures, and work closely with senior mentors to learn and apply industry-standard clean architecture and testing patterns.

Qualifications

  • Currently working towards a Bachelor, Masters, or PhD degree in Computer Science, Robotics, or equivalent.
  • Self-starter comfortable working in a fast paced, technically challenging startup environment.
  • Strong background in: linear algebra, Python, data science, and data structures / algorithms.
  • Strong communication skills that clearly express ideas and design details in meetings, team presentations, white board brainstorming sessions and in various technical documentation.
  • Prioritize organization and detail orientation, with ability to handle multiple project and task assignments simultaneously.
  • Passionate, curious, and eager to learn.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with robotic systems.
  • Experience with cloud technologies, specifically AWS.
  • Industry experience with Python.

Total Rewards & Life at Multiply Labs

  • Competitive Compensation: $5,000-$7,000/month.

  • Real Ownership: Own meaningful design projects on robots that go into production, not side tasks.

  • Mentorship: Work side by side with experienced mechanical, robotics, and software engineers.

  • Office Perks: An energetic SF office culture featuring catered team lunches, stocked kitchen, and frequent team events.

  • Great people, meaningful work, and a team that genuinely believes in what we’re building.

  • No Set Hours: Set your own schedule in alignment with your manager and team. We hold a high bar, measuring success by impact and outcomes—not hours logged.

Come build the world’s best robots—and help make life-saving therapies accessible to all.

We actively seek candidates with diverse perspectives and lived experiences. We’re committed to building a team where everyone feels valued, respected, and empowered to do their best work.

Multiply Labs encourages candidates from all backgrounds to apply—even if you don’t meet every qualification. If you’re excited about our mission and think you can contribute, we’d love to hear from you.

Our headquarters is located in San Francisco’s vibrant Dogpatch neighborhood.

title: Salesforce Administrator
description:
Salesforce Administrator

Team: Sales Operations

Location: Fully remote, Spain or Poland

Reports to: Head of Sales Ops

The short version

Our sales, account management and partnerships teams deal with our most important customers and partners. Sales Ops is the team that builds, improves and maintains the tools and processes they use to succeed.

We are looking for a hands-on Salesforce administrator to keep our commercial teams productive through responsive day-to-day support, access management, data quality and platform maintenance. You'll also help maintain reporting and develop your automation and AI skills alongside our Salesforce Developer.

What you'll do

Be the first point of contact for Salesforce support. Triage and resolve internal support tickets, including duplicate records, data clean-up, validation issues, access problems and minor bugs. Escalate more complex issues to our Salesforce Developer or Data Ops team, ensuring users receive timely support.

Manage day-to-day Salesforce administration. Maintain users, permission sets, sharing rules, page layouts, fields and validation across our sales, partnerships and account management processes. Help safeguard sensitive customer data by keeping access controls accurate.

Support smaller configuration and automation improvements. Handle straightforward changes to validation rules, record types and Flows, working with our Salesforce Developer on more complex builds. We don't use the Lead object. Everything runs on Account, Contact and Opportunity, which means the Opportunity model carries a lot of weight and needs care.

Maintain and improve Salesforce reports and dashboards. Keep everyday reporting accurate for sales teams and managers, fix minor filtering issues, and tidy up legacy reports that are no longer useful.

Get to the answer in the data. Use basic SOQL queries to investigate affected records and troubleshoot everyday support tickets when standard reports don't provide the answer.

Keep the connected stack healthy. Outreach, Modjo, Kubaru, Lusha, Clay, Hightouch and other tools. You don't need to arrive an expert in each, but you should be the person who knows where the data comes from and identify what breaks when it stops.

Push the vision forward. We want all day-to-day sales work to happen in Salesforce: The data they need to see, the actions they need to take, and the AI and automation solutions that multiply their productivity. You help get us there, alongside our Salesforce Developer and Data Ops Analyst.

How we build

Three principles guide everything we ship:

Top user experience. Minimise admin work for our users, maximise their productivity. Their time is the point.

Build it right. Efficient, scalable, adaptable. We dislike technical debt and we don't pretend it isn't there.

Security and privacy. Customer and prospect data safety is not a checkbox at the end of a project, it's a foundational requirement in everything we do.

What you bring

  • 1+ years of hands-on Salesforce administration experience with Sales Cloud or Service Cloud, supporting a live business team.

  • Practical Salesforce administration skills: user management, validation rules, permission sets and sharing, plus basic reports and dashboards.

  • Experience maintaining Salesforce reports and dashboards, including fixing filters and improving existing reporting.

  • Basic SOQL. You can write straightforward queries to inspect records and troubleshoot everyday support issues.

  • You can turn a vague request into a spec, and you push back when the request is the wrong fix for the real problem.

  • An obsession with making your Salesforce users happy. This is not a back-office role. You will hear directly when something is annoying, and you should want to hear it.

  • Fluent English. Our team and company include people from many European countries, English is our common language.

  • You love independence and hold yourself accountable. This is a full remote position and micromanagement is not something we do

Bonus points

  • Experience with AI tools such as Agentforce or Claude, or an interest in developing these skills.

  • Experience designing Salesforce report types and dashboards for different audiences.

  • Salesforce Administrator certification (ADM-201); Advanced Admin or Platform App Builder on top of it.

  • Experience with Outreach, Clay, Hightouch or Kubaru.

  • SQL, and experience with Databricks, Bigquery or Snowflake.

  • Enough Apex literacy to read and understand what our developer wrote.

  • Experience working in Fintech, banking or other highly regulated environments.

title: Impact Intelligence Product Manager
description:
This position is fully remote. The ideal candidate may be located anywhere in the continental United States.

A Day in the Life of a Product Manager, Impact Intelligence at MetLife Legal Plans:

The Impact Intelligence team is seeking a Product Manager who can operate fluently at the intersection of business strategy, analytics, and data engineering. This role will partner with business stakeholders to understand the decision or outcome behind a data request, translate that need into clear and testable requirements, and guide the Impact Intelligence team in delivering trusted, reusable data products and insights.

The successful candidate will connect business context with technical execution. They will clarify ambiguous requests, define value and priority, align stakeholders on scope and acceptance criteria, and communicate effectively with executives, business partners, data analysts, analytics engineers, and data engineers.

Responsibilities (Essential Duties and Responsibilities):

  • Engage business partners to understand the business objective, decisions to be supported, target audience, measures of success, constraints, and urgency behind each request.
  • Translate business questions into well-defined epics, features, user stories, data requirements, business rules, acceptance criteria, and nonfunctional requirements that the Impact Intelligence team can execute.
  • Facilitate discovery sessions that surface source systems, grain, dimensions, facts, hierarchies, calculation logic, data quality expectations, security considerations, and refresh needs.
  • Partner with data analysts, analytics engineers, and data engineers to shape solutions that are valuable, feasible, scalable, secure, and maintainable.
  • Own and prioritize the product backlog using business value, strategic alignment, customer impact, risk, dependencies, data readiness, and delivery effort.
  • Lead backlog refinement, sprint planning, reviews, stakeholder demonstrations, and retrospectives in partnership with the delivery team.
  • Define and maintain a clear product roadmap for Impact Intelligence capabilities, balancing near-term business needs with reusable enterprise data assets.
  • Ensure requirements preserve metric consistency and common business definitions across semantic models, dashboards, analyses, and downstream use cases.
  • Validate delivered capabilities with business partners, confirm acceptance criteria, coordinate user acceptance testing, and drive adoption through clear release communication and enablement.
  • Monitor product outcomes and stakeholder feedback, then use evidence to improve prioritization, data products, and team ways of working.
  • Identify and manage dependencies, risks, scope changes, and trade-offs; escalate decisions with concise options and impact statements.
  • Communicate technical concepts in business terms and business needs in data terms, adapting depth and language to the audience.

Minimum Qualifications (Knowledge, skills, and abilities required)

  • 5+ years of experience in product management, product ownership, business analysis, data and analytics, or a related role, including experience delivering data or analytics products.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous business needs into clear requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, process flows, and prioritized backlogs.
  • Working knowledge of dimensional data modeling, including facts, dimensions, grain, keys, slowly changing dimensions, and semantic or metrics layers.
  • Working knowledge of modern data warehousing concepts, including ingestion, transformation, orchestration, data lineage, data quality, metadata, and governed access.
  • Strong data analysis skills and proficiency using SQL to explore data, validate requirements, investigate issues, and assess delivered outcomes.
  • Practical experience with Agile and Scrum methods, including discovery, backlog management, refinement, sprint planning, reviews, retrospectives, and incremental delivery.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with both technical and nontechnical audiences, including senior leaders, business subject-matter experts, analysts, and engineers.
  • Excellent facilitation, problem-solving, prioritization, negotiation, and written communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment while managing multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.
  • Understanding data governance, privacy, security, and data quality principles as they apply to analytics products.

What Will Make You Special (Preferred knowledge, skills, and abilities):

  • Experience with cloud data platforms and analytics tools such as Amazon Redshift, DBT Cloud, Tableau, GitHub, or Jira.
  • Knowledge and hands-on experience applying AI capabilities within DBT and Tableau, such as DBT's AI-assisted development features and Tableau's Pulse, Einstein Copilot, or similar generative analytics tools.
  • Experience using external generative AI tools such as Microsoft Copilot or Claude to accelerate requirements writing, documentation, data analysis, and other product management tasks.
  • Skilled at describing and illustrating complex data concepts for varied audiences using tools such as PowerPoint, Word, and AI visual generation tools.
  • Experience defining or managing semantic models, certified data sets, dashboards, metrics, or self-service analytics products.
  • Experience supporting business domains such as customer enrollment, retention, operations, finance, sales, service, or digital product analytics.
  • Product Owner or Agile certification such as CSPO, PSPO, PMI-ACP, or SAFe POPM.
  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited university or equivalent relevant experience.
  • Ability to communicate complex concepts with written or visual tools as well as skills with the latest AI tools and capabilities as it related to data activities

Travel

Optional travel to team meetups.


Who We Are:

MetLife Legal Plans is the country's largest provider of legal voluntary benefits. We have more than 40 years of experience in employee legal services and are committed to providing excellent care to our plan members, sponsors and 18,000+ attorneys.

We are trusted by nearly 7 million families and more than 200 Fortune 500 companies who offer our service as an employee benefit.

It’s an exciting time to join our team. We are growing quickly and have a bold vision for our future as we evolve our company to dream bigger, move faster, and use creativity and technology to build products people love.

MLP's Core 4:

  • Put customers first

title: Network Engineer
description:
Are you looking for a challenging yet rewarding job that allows you to utilize your skills to their fullest potential? Do you want to join a team of hardworking, enthusiastic and creative people and enjoy working with a company that recognizes and embraces diversity? Do you take pride working with a company that is committed to being a great corporate citizen and playing a role in producing the highest quality products and services?

If you answered yes to any of these questions, then Pridgeon and Clay is the place for you...

Founded in 1948 by John Pridgeon and Donald Clay, we are one of the largest independent, value-added manufacturers and suppliers of automotive stamped and fine-blanked components in the United States.

Objective: The Network Engineer is responsible for analyzing, designing, installing, configuring, maintaining and repairing the network infrastructure and application components, including the corporate Operational Data Centers, and redundant systems. A Network Engineer performs a wide variety of evaluation, maintenance, installation and training tasks to ensure the computer network performance meets company and user satisfaction. A Network Engineer also provides direction, information, and recommendations regarding network configurations and installations.

Qualified candidates will possess the following Minimum Requirements:

  • 4 Year college degree in a computer-related field with a minimum of five(5) years IT industry experience required
  • Global WAN infrastructure knowledge and Cisco networking experience required
  • Microsoft Exchange and/or SQL experience required
  • Knowledge of VoIP implementation and support required
  • Knowledge of Virtual Machine/Thin Client implementation(s) required.
  • Knowledge of network security through proper configuration of VPN and Firewalls required
  • Ability to communicate both written and verbal required
  • Must have demonstrated good problem solving and analytical skills to resolve complex tactical, technical, and business related issues.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to multi-task in a global enterprise business environment
  • Availability to respond to needs of the end user for installation, maintenance and equipment malfunctions as required
  • Demonstrated growth potential, by having achieved previously established goals, learning new skills, and proven strategic thinking.

Outstanding candidates will possess the following Desired Requirements:

  • Microsoft System Center experience a plus
  • Basic programming/scripting knowledge.
  • Current CCNA, CCNP and/or MCSE certifications a plus
  • VMWare knowledge and experience a plus
  • Citrix Server/ CISCO blade service management experience a plus
  • Service Delivery and ITIL Methodologies a plus
  • Experience working in cross functional teams using agile methodologies
  • Cisco Unified Communication Manager configuration and infrastructure experience required

(Minimum requirements are updated annually to meet the demands of various positions; employees hired prior to the latest revision update may not meet all current requirements.)

Essential Functions:

Network Engineering:

  • Maintain a thorough understanding of the basics behind the Internet and its workings (DNS, Security, IP Routing, HTTP, VPN, Email Routing, SPAM, etc.)
  • Operate, enhance and maintain the global data centers and its operating systems (VMWare, Linux, Windows Server)
  • Configure and setup Cisco Firewalls, VPN Concentrators and Security appliances for access to vital business applications
  • Design, setup and configure switching environments
  • Design, setup and configure wireless networking that supports open or secured access and the ability to support voice and video applications
  • Develop a thorough understanding of Local Area Networking
  • Assist in the design of multi-server environments including IP address schemes, DNS, & WINS
  • Configuring and installing client and server network software for upgrading and maintaining network and telecommunication systems
  • Continually work to achieve business objectives and meet the objectives measureable.

Hardware Support:

  • Troubleshooting malfunctions of network hardware and software applications, telephones and security systems to resolve operational issues and restore services
  • Supervising the administration of systems and servers related to network to ensure availability of services to authorized users
  • Maintaining multi-site network operations and software applications, operating systems and regular maintenance with both private and public facilities
  • Critically evaluate information gathered from multiple sources, reconcile conflicts, assemble high-level information into details, abstract up from low-level information to a general understanding, and distinguish user requests from the underlying true business needs.

Project Management:

  • Successfully manage in 1-2 significant project initiatives simultaneously and business case creation as needed with minimal direction.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills and the ability to interact professionally with a diverse group, executives, managers, and subject matter experts.
  • Proactively communicate and collaborate with external and internal customers to analyze infrastructure needs.

Individual Objectives:

  • Utilize prior experience with enterprise-wide architecture to define and change current methodologies.
  • Continually work to achieve individual objectives that improve skills and capability.

Teamwork/Professionalism:

  • Consistently contribute to the success of the cross-functional SCRUM teams and co-worker's objects.
  • Provide necessary, accurate, and timely feedback of all pertinent information to co-workers and management to enhance teamwork and communication initiatives.
  • Consistently exhibit appropriate attendance habits, working the necessary hours to perform the job.
  • Organize and maintain efficiency of personal work area and department.
  • Consistently adhere to, and support, company policies and procedures, including ISO, TS16949, and safety regulations.
  • Accept instructions and duties in a positive manner. Perform any other activities as directed by the Information Technology leadership.
  • Treat all co-workers with dignity and respect. Exhibit all the attributes of a positive role model (including professionalism, personal integrity, and positive attitude) for employees and managers to emulate.
  • Assist in maintaining company values (Integrity, People, Customers, Ownership, We Can If..., Safety) daily, through thoughts and actions.

In return, Pridgeon and Clay will provide:

  • A competitive total compensation including a comprehensive benefit plan including premium medical and prescription coverage starting at just $5.00 per week for employee coverage, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement.
  • A safe, team oriented work environment with a leadership team that treats you like family and values your input
  • An opportunity to participate in shaping the success of the organization through continuous improvement and problem solving events
  • A positive work/life balance
  • An opportunity for career growth – Over 70% of our leaders have been promoted from within

title: IT Operations & Cybersecurity Specialist
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an IT Operations & Cybersecurity Specialist based in France.

Join a distributed technology team dedicated to delivering reliable IT operations and strengthening cybersecurity for organisations that handle sensitive data. In this remote, hands-on role, you will manage day-to-day IT administration, support users, and maintain secure digital environments for multiple clients. You will work with modern cloud productivity platforms, endpoint management tools, and automation technologies to ensure systems remain secure, compliant, and operational. Beyond routine IT support, you will contribute to security initiatives involving vulnerability research, device hardening, and incident response documentation. This position offers an opportunity to develop your cybersecurity expertise while taking ownership of operational responsibilities. You will thrive in an autonomous, asynchronous working environment that values reliability, continuous learning, and practical problem-solving.

Accountabilities

  • IT Administration: Provision and manage user accounts, groups, permissions, and licences across Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, ensuring secure and efficient access to business applications.
  • Endpoint Management: Prepare and onboard Windows and macOS laptops into mobile device management (MDM) platforms, coordinate remote device handovers, and maintain appropriate device configurations.
  • Technical Support: Handle first-line support requests, including password resets, access issues, and routine troubleshooting, while escalating more complex incidents when necessary.
  • IT Maintenance and Monitoring: Conduct weekly maintenance checks covering software patch status, backup logs, security alerts, and general system health to help maintain reliable operations.
  • Documentation and Process Improvement: Document technical fixes, standard operating procedures, and runbooks to improve consistency, knowledge sharing, and operational efficiency.
  • Cybersecurity Projects: Dedicate approximately 20% of your time to security-focused initiatives, including CVE research and briefings, laptop hardening scripts, incident-response playbooks, and ISO 27001 checklist development.
  • Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities to streamline IT workflows, strengthen security practices, and improve service delivery across a distributed client environment.

Requirements

  • Professional Experience: At least two years of hands-on experience in IT operations, helpdesk support, systems administration, or a comparable technical role.
  • Cloud Administration: Practical experience administering Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, including user and group management, security policies, permissions, and basic troubleshooting.
  • Endpoint Management: Familiarity with MDM solutions such as Microsoft Intune, Jamf, or equivalent platforms, including device enrolment and configuration.
  • Scripting and Automation: Proficiency in at least one scripting language, such as PowerShell, Bash, or Python, with the ability to automate routine tasks and improve operational workflows.
  • Communication Skills: Strong written and spoken English, with the ability to document technical processes clearly and collaborate effectively with distributed teams. German language skills are an advantage.
  • Remote Working Readiness: A reliable internet connection, a professional remote working environment, and the ability to work independently across different time zones.
  • Personal Attributes: A proactive, organised, and detail-oriented approach, with strong troubleshooting skills, sound judgement, and a willingness to learn and take ownership of responsibilities.
  • Preferred Qualifications: Microsoft 365 Administrator Expert, Microsoft 365 Endpoint Administrator, or Google Workspace Administrator certifications are advantageous.
  • Security Knowledge: Exposure to cybersecurity and compliance frameworks such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, or similar standards is a plus.

Benefits

  • Competitive Compensation: Hourly compensation within the advertised range of €10–€18, with the original role description specifying a typical rate of €12–€16 per hour, paid in euros.
  • Fully Remote Work: Work remotely from anywhere.
  • Autonomy and Ownership: Take responsibility for your area of work, manage your tasks independently, and contribute directly to operational improvements.
  • Professional Development: Build practical cybersecurity experience through hands-on projects involving vulnerability research, endpoint hardening, incident response, and compliance.
  • Career Growth: Opportunity to expand your responsibilities and progress into a broader role as the team grows.
  • Flexible, Asynchronous Culture: Benefit from an async-first working environment, with occasional video meetings scheduled during hours compatible with Central European Time (CET).
  • Practical Security Experience: Develop your technical capabilities while working across IT administration, endpoint management, automation, and security operations.
